## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. - code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. - fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). - anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). - security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.

- [Watch loops must not match themselves](watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves.md) — `pgrep -f` sees the polling shell and hangs forever; `ps -eo args` truncates at 80 columns, so wait on the PID.
- [Benchmark runs in strix-halo-vulkan](strix-halo-bench-runs.md) — the flags, the wall-clock, and the two-run reproducibility convention.
- [Phase order: verticals, not experiments](phase-2-pivot-to-pipeline.md) — build a thing that runs, profile, then optimise; z-image parked 2026-09-14 for the speech verticals in `research/speech-vertical.md`.
- [Reference dumps: the Python env](reference-dumps-python-env.md) — no pip in `.venv`; use `uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python`.
- [Auto-committer owns main](auto-committer-owns-main.md) — commits land as `ai` on a timer, and other sessions edit the same tree, so a build break may not be yours.
- [The whole-model runs take the machine](llm-resident-run.md) — `-resident`/`-graph`/`-gen`/TestGraphLogits are 84-85 GB and ~35-50 s; use the 4-layer prefix while iterating.
- [Mapped GPU arenas: read vs write](vulkan-mapped-arena-reads.md) — the host reads a write-combined Vulkan buffer at 0.18 GB/s.
- [Deployment is two machines](deployment-two-machines.md) — LLM alone on one, the rest on the other; no footprint quantisation for the small verticals.
- [Debugging a hung GPU run](gpu-debugging-access.md) — no sudo/dmesg/debugfs; journalctl -k, /proc utime-vs-stime, and gdb must be the ancestor.
- [The ai server is a user systemd unit](ai-service-user-unit.md) — `journalctl --user -u ai`, deploy.sh installs it, ~25 s to come up; omitting `-token` does NOT disable auth, and it is served open on purpose.
- [Running the MTP draft head](mtp-draft-head-run.md) — `cmd/llm -mtp` is ~80 GB, and `-mtp-free` degenerates into a loop that reads as +18 points of acceptance.
- [Running the speculative loop](spec-loop-run.md) — `cmd/llm -spec` is parked at 0.95x; set the shipped banks or you measure the wrong model.
- [A new row count needs a graph gate](two-row-regime-needs-a-graph-gate.md) — block tests passed while a two-token pass was 45x wrong.
- [Benchmarks need LLM_BANK_CACHE](llm-bench-needs-bank-cache.md) — `cmd/llm` never sets it, so a shipped-bank run re-fits for 8 minutes on 32 cores.
- [Prefill out to 128k](long-context-prefill-128k.md) — P17 heads-on-rows takes it to 1011 tok/s at ubatch 2048, 1176 at 4096; P14's changes and refusals below it.
- [Decode at depth (P15, P16)](decode-at-depth-after-p15.md) — the table that stands for decode: 34.4 tok/s at depth zero, 31.5 at 128k; the wide-batch cost was a padding bug found by a per-label diff.
- [The arena's memory type is free](vulkan-arena-memory-type-is-free.md) — HOST_CACHED costs the GPU nothing at 3.85 GB; stop suspecting it.
- [Rates against context depth](context-depth-rates.md) — P7+P8+P9+P10 closed it: 64k decode 4.05 → 27.69 tok/s, falloff 0.14x → 0.79x; the five gates and the control env vars.
- [Docs consolidated into research/](docs-consolidated-into-research.md) — 2026-09-20: root progress files are frozen archives in `research/`; `TODO.md` is the live state of play, and `CONCURRENCY.md` (C-stages) is live for P6.
- [Image vertical: Qwen-Image-2.1](image-vertical-qwen-image-21.md) — served (gen + `-edits N`), archive `research/qimage-vertical.md`; Q13 int8 banks default (31.5 → 20.4 GB, encoder keeps layers 6/16 fp16, priced vs bf16 dumps); Q14 previews via taesd's TAEQI2.1 (models/taeqi2_1, normalized latent), transformers 5.17.0 + diffusers git 80c7ed26 for dumps.
- [Decode is latency, not bandwidth](decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth.md) — 24 single-wave workgroups all fit at once, so only the length of one wave's loop matters.
- [Never edit source during a sweep](never-edit-source-during-a-sweep.md) — `go run` rebuilds per arm; build once to the scratchpad under a per-sweep name, and check ps before starting a second GPU run.
- [GraphStats.Kinds aliases the live graph](graphstats-kinds-aliases.md) — a kept snapshot keeps absorbing dispatches; only the last depth of a sweep was ever right.
- [Prefill rates and what bounds them](prefill-rates.md) — the ubatch curve, why a wider `-llm-batch` now costs only memory (P16), and four prefill ideas that are measured dead.
- [A benchmark that gets faster](a-benchmark-that-gets-faster.md) — maxStorageBufferRange is silent when exceeded, so runs come back fast and wrong; hit by the llm arena and by the DiT arena at `-edits 3`.
- [Three ways the llm test suite misleads](llm-test-suite-gotchas.md) — a 10-minute timeout, a TestGraphLogits failure that is not yours, and 23 GB in llm/models.
- [Full 262k context (P18)](llm-full-context-262k.md) — KV cache is a buffer a plane (a set a slot since C6); ai.service LLM line is -llm-ctx 262144 -llm-batch 8192 -llm-slots 3, ~98 GB; ppl 4.0344 at 131k-262k.
- [The concurrency load generator](concurrency-loadgen-run.md) — cmd/loadgen, one server restart per arm (~4.5 min), worst voice wait is one chunk, not the sampled arrivals.
- [Batched rows need distinct conversations](batched-rows-need-distinct-conversations.md) — one sequence's rows share experts; price C5 with `cmd/llm -batch` (greedy, a slot a row), 3 rows = 53 ms after the moe.up fix.
- [WMMA sums see the sign of a zero](wmma-negative-zero-products.md) — a -0 product behind a +0 mask moves the result an ulp; hit by the LLM pack and by Kev K7.7 — zero V padding, and test a "layout" residue with a junk-filled KV cache first.
- [Batched rows run side by side](batched-rows-overlap.md) — per-row attn/DN dispatches overlap; group time lands on the first dispatch; LLM_BATCH_OVERLAP=0 is the control.
- [LLM vision vertical](llm-vision-vertical.md) — root `LLM-VISION.md` is live (V0-V10 and V12 done, served via `-llm-mmproj`; the V10 eval ties llama.cpp at 17/18; the tower yields every 50 ms); HF over vLLM on positions, image drift is MoE routing ties, reuse keyed per picture.
- [Classification vertical: Kev-4B](classification-vertical-kev.md) — root `CLASSIFICATION.md` live (K0–K6, K7.1 int8 bank, K7.2 prefix cache, K7.3 WMMA attention, K7.4 l8 scan, K7.5 batching, K7.6 GLU fusion, K7.7 (bit-exact: stale V padding) and K8 (card reproduced, int8 −0.19 pp) done 2026-09-25, K9 scheduler + parallel head + chunked streams 2026-09-28 (`cmd/kevload`), `-kev` serves `/v1/systemone`); Kev's code vendored as the oracle; noul/[no,yes]/fim_suffix traps
- [Video vertical: MiniMax-H3](video-vertical-minimax-h3.md) — root `VIDEO.md` live (M-stages; M0–M10 + M11a done 2026-09-26: prompt (+ keyframes) → mp4, `serve -video` answers `/v1/videos`; M11a int8 banks by default, measured request peak 31 GB, priced against bf16 not fp16; M11b bank-cache/ cuts staging ~94 → 12 s; M11c transposed attention, no LDS for P, forward 1.16x/1.30x; M11d split-K down proj, bit-identical, 1.02x; M11e VAE attention transposed at head 64, decode 1.035x; M11f GPU audio priced ≤2.4 s, not built; M12 prompt rewrite is the client's), code in `h3/`, `api/videos.go`, `backend/video.go`; gates teacher-forced or perceptual
- [API follows OpenAI's standard](api-follows-openai-standard.md) — behaviour, not just shape: fetch image URLs wherever OpenAI fetches them; check the OpenAI reference before inventing a rule.
- [Server memory is not standalone memory](server-memory-is-not-standalone-memory.md) — a request that fits standalone OOM-killed ai.service: the server's big live heap sets a big GC target; measure served, 20 ms sampler, a kill guard, nothing else running.
- [Music vertical: ACE-Step 1.5](music-vertical-ace-step.md) — closed 2026-09-27, record in `research/music-vertical.md` (code cites `MUSIC.md` A-stages); VAE encoder needs fp16 hi+lo pairs (compiler folds the naive split); covers ride on FSQ code flips; oracle = upstream in `.venv-acestep`
- [Swap slot: image, music, video](swap-slot-image-music-video.md) — one residency slot, -swap-idle 10m; 9.4 GB at rest, 60 GB worst vs ~112 all-resident; staging makes zero queue submits (STAGE_GPU=1 test).
- [OCR vertical: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6](ocr-vertical-paddleocr-vl.md) — root `OCR.md` live (O0–O10 + O11a done; O10 OmniDocBench subset: Go 96.13 = PaddleX 96.14, card 96.34; O11a batched decode over a paged KV cache, subset 66 → 18 min same score; next O11b towers/tail); ERNIE = ace/lm shaders rebuilt; oracle `reference/dump_ocr.py` (align_corners=False); eval in the OmniDocBench Docker image via `reference/omnidocbench_eval.sh`
- [Kev speed: sole workload](kev-speed-assumes-sole-workload.md) — tune classification as if it's alone on the machine; device-lock clashes with image etc. are out of scope.
- [Embeddings E7 batching](embedding-vertical-e7.md) — done 2026-09-28, deployed 2026-09-29: RunBatch bit-exact, served round-robin worker, 128 texts 1535 → 305 ms; never take the model lock on the request path.
- [Kernels vertical reopened](kernels-vertical-reopened.md) — root `KERNELS.md` (G-stages) 2026-09-29: G0–G2, G5a/b/c/d and G4 (2026-09-30, attention at its plateau, next G6 or G3) done (MoE up GEMM's K loop pipelined, 1.68x, prefill 1194 → 1407 tok/s; G5c 2026-09-30 short last tile, prefill 1417 → 1514, m2/m4 boundary now 256 tokens); the GEMM ships as LDS-staged slabs at wave32 (`dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32`, 74 → 80% per clock, H3 480p forward 29.9 → 27.1 s), carried to all nine hosts (G8) the same day; it loses below ~1000 rows, so ace/dit keeps the wave64 build there.
- [Coopmat fragments cost 8 VGPRs](coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs.md) — 4x replicated at wave64, ACO copies a loop-carried fragment as v_mov_b16s, LDS coopmat reads are ds_load_b64 (pitch 36 halves); register prefetch of fragments is dead on Mesa 26.2.2.
- [H3 GEMM screen recipe](h3-gemm-screen-recipe.md) — H3_GEMM_SPV/WAVE/KRANGE_SPV/REF on TestGPUShapes with the hwmon sampler: 2.5 min, real shapes, real clock, bit-identical gate.
- [LDS GEMM needs a full machine](lds-gemm-needs-a-full-machine.md) — the wave32 LDS-staged GEMM loses 8–11% under ~40 workgroups (~1000 rows); ace/dit switches to the wave64 build at 1024 rows, and any new host must screen its short inputs.
- [VALU costs matrix clocks](valu-costs-matrix-clocks.md) — a WMMA kernel pays ~1 pipe clock per VALU instruction; count `v_swap`/`v_mov` per MMA in the ISA before timing; the LDS GEMM ships its K tiles as a loop for +5 points.
- [MoE GEMM screening](moe-gemm-screening.md) — `LLM_MOE_SPV` loads a grouped-GEMM build from disk; run the `llm` tests from `llm/` or they SKIP-as-PASS; a `-moe` arm is ~2 s of GPU so quote the clock median above 100 W.
- [Attention kernel plateau](attention-kernel-plateau.md) — no exact arm beats the shipped transposed attention (softmax 7, K/V loads 12, floor 81%); the allocator decides; the image DiT's edit gate sits near its sensitivity floor, so perturb the passing path first.
- [Control arms move the clock](control-arms-move-the-clock.md) — a store-free GEMM arm read +9% that was all clock (downstream kernels on zeros at 130 W); compare per clock, leave stale data not zeros.

1	# KERNELS — the matrix cores to their ceiling
2	
3	> **Live tracking and session handoff doc, opened 2026-09-29.** Stage
4	> letters are **G** (GEMM; K is classification, W and R are speech). This
5	> is the project's first vertical, reopened: not a model, but the kernels
6	> every vertical stands on. A closed finding still gets a `§N.M` number and
7	> a file in `research/` as before (README there: the number is the address,
8	> never renumber); the G-stage here is where it is tracked while open. When
9	> the vertical closes, this file is frozen to `research/kernels-vertical.md`.
10	
11	## What we are building
12	
13	`GOALS.md`'s first sentence: *the most efficient ways to run these models
14	on Vulkan on this part*. Every vertical since has been a model brought up
15	on the kernels this one produced, and each of them ended on the same
16	sentence: "the GEMMs are at their ceiling, the bigger fish is elsewhere".
17	That ceiling was **42.0 TFLOP/s against a measured 55.5**, and it has not
18	moved since stage 4 (2026-09-21). Eight verticals later, the matrix cores
19	are the one place where a win lands in *every* served request at once: a
20	480p video forward is 63% GEMM and 33% attention on these kernels, an
21	image step 72% GEMM, a prefill chunk mostly GEMM. **A 1.15x on the GEMM is
22	worth more than any single vertical's remaining backlog.**
23	
24	The deliverable is three kernel classes at a higher fraction of the
25	per-clock ceiling than today, carried into the verticals through the
26	screens they already have, and the ceiling itself pinned better than it
27	is:
28	
29	| class | file | today | target |
30	|---|---|---|---|
31	| fp16 WMMA GEMM (activation × fp16 weight) | `shaders/dit_gemm.comp` (the vertical kernel), `shaders/gemm_wmma.comp` (the ablation suite) | 39.0 suite / **42.0** pipeline, 72–78% | ≥ 85% per clock |
32	| WMMA flash attention | `shaders/h3_attn_t.comp` (transposed, wave32), `shaders/dit_attention_wmma.comp` (plain) | **37.3–37.8** at 2650–2690 MHz, **73%** per clock (G4, §3.8: the floor with the softmax gutted is 81%, 87–90% with L0 hits; no exact arm beats the shipped build) | ≥ 80% |
33	| int8 / Q4-weight WMMA GEMM | `shaders/llm_moe_gemm.comp`, `shaders/llm_gemm.comp`, `shaders/kev_gemm_q8_glu.comp`, `dit_dequant_q8` + fp16 GEMM (video) | MoE Q4 up: 22 → **37 TFLOP/s executed** at 2048 tokens (§2.11, ~75% per clock; 51% in §2.2), down 19–21, the rest unmeasured against the ceiling | the fp16 GEMM's rate at the same M, N, K |
34	| streaming kernels (norms, packs, gates, SwiGLU, copies) | everywhere | 6–14% of every block; `hc.cn` at 134 GB/s (TODO); H3's SwiGLU and v pack fused into the GEMM's epilogue (G3, §2.14) | ≥ 200 GB/s each, or fused away |
35	
36	Decode is not in the table: §1.7–§1.12 took the GEMV to 96–103% of the
37	bus, and the LLM's decode has been a *format* question since (L8).
38	
39	## What we did (the record, so it is not re-run)
40	
41	The kernel work of 2026-09-13 to 09-21 is filed under `§N.M` in
42	`research/ideas.md` and its per-item files. The ladder, on the fp16 GEMM:
43	
44	| step | lever | best GEMM | of 55.5 | file |
45	|---|---|---|---|---|
46	| §0 | the ceilings measured on this chip, not extrapolated | — | — | `0-measurement-validity.md` |
47	| baseline | one 16×16 accumulator a wave, `gemm_coopmat_fp16.comp` | 4.9 | 9% | |
48	| §2.1 | register blocking: a WM×WN accumulator grid a wave (AI 8 → 32) | 25.2 | 45% | `2.1-register-blocking.md` |
49	| §2.3 | padded leading dimensions: a K-strided fragment load off one DRAM channel | 28.4 | 51% | `2.3-channel-aliasing.md` |
50	| §2.7 | a whole K-slab's fragment loads in flight before its first MMA | 39.0 | 70% | `2.7-kslab-hoist.md` |
51	| §2.8 | the weight stored as 16×16 fragment tiles (packed once at upload) | 41.0 on two of three shapes | 74% | `stage-4-dit-graph.md` |
52	| §2.4 | the grid walked in bands of 8 columns (MALL locality) | **42.0 / 41.1 / 40.6** on the DiT's three shapes | 73–76% | `stage-4-dit-graph.md` |
53	
54	And on the others:
55	
56	- **Attention** (§3.3, `stage-3-dit-attention.md`): both matmuls on the
57	  matrix cores, online softmax, every operand as fragment tiles: 1.28 →
58	  **38.8 TFLOP/s** (30x), wave32 a clean 1.40x over wave64 at the same
59	  tiling. Then VIDEO.md **M11c**: the LDS round trip that turned P from an
60	  accumulator into an operand was ~60% of the kernel; computing S^T and
61	  O^T instead puts P^T on the B side with one shuffle per element pair, no
62	  LDS, no barrier, 1.55–1.61x on H3's kernel. M11e carried it to head 64.
63	- **Q4 weights on the matrix cores** (§2.2): 2.10x a MoE block, at **51%**
64	  of the matrix cores, because the operand must round-trip through LDS
65	  ("no extension exposes a fragment's lane layout"). **That premise is now
66	  false**: M11c's `coopmat_layout_probe.comp` reads the element order back
67	  and it is fixed and simple on this device.
68	- **Grouped MoE GEMM** (§3.5): 1.1–4.1x, and the mechanism was occupancy.
69	- **conv2d as an implicit GEMM** (stage 8): conv3x3 at **41–42 TFLOP/s**;
70	  the dilated 1-D convolutions of kokoro's vocoder on `dit_gemm`'s
71	  `A_CONV` at 22.4.
72	- **Decode GEMV** (§1.1, §1.7–§1.12): 96–103% of the 236 GB/s bus at
73	  every N; done.
74	- **Wave size** (§6.2): a per-pipeline knob; the GEMM spills at wave32 and
75	  loses, the fragment-dominated kernels gain 1.4–2.1x.
76	- **The ISA** (§6.1): `cmd/probe` + `RADV_DEBUG=asm|shaderstats`. It found
77	  §2.3 (a row-major B fragment is sixteen scalar loads). **It was deleted
78	  by accident on 2026-09-22** (collateral in a speech commit, README still
79	  documented it) and **restored today**.
80	
81	**Refused, measured, so not to be re-run without a new reason:** LDS
82	staging of A/B slabs (§2.1, lost at every tile; the MALL supplies the
83	reuse), LDS double-buffering (same), split-K on the big shapes (M11d: two K
84	passes buy 1.02x on `down` only because its A chunk overflows the MALL,
85	and a chunk of 4096 gets the same without it), swizzle bands other than 8
86	(§2.4, M11d), A row pads other than 128 (M11d), QT4 and KTIL8 attention
87	builds (spill), the lane-split row max (P12-1, slower everywhere), wave32
88	for the register-blocked GEMM (spills, −25%), an int8 *kernel* where the
89	GEMM is compute-bound (WMMA int8 runs at the fp16 rate, §0.1).
90	
91	## What we have today
92	
93	The ceiling, restated per clock, because the clock moves under load:
94	
95	| | rate | sclk | power | FLOP/clk/CU |
96	|---|---|---|---|---|
97	| spec, 512 FLOP/clk/CU × 40 × 2.9 GHz | 59.4 | 2900 | | 512 |
98	| `peak` probe, wmma_fp16, wave64, 8 chains (`results/peak.csv`) | **55.5** | 2899 | 107–119 W | **478** |
99	| best suite GEMM, `wmma_reg64_bt_hka4_padab128` at 2048³ | 39.0 | **2813** | **137 W** | 347 (72.6%) |
100	| best pipeline GEMM, `dit_gemm_wg128x256_bt16_swz8` on `dit.qkv` at M = 4096 | 42.0 | *not recorded* | | 362–373 (76–78%) |
101	| H3's GEMMs, 480p (VIDEO.md M11h) | 37–38 | not recorded | | ~70% |
102	| H3's GEMMs on `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` (G2, §2.9) | 40.7–41.1 (down 40.8) | 2665 | 154 | 385 (80%) |
103	| **… with the K tiles as a loop (G-o8, §2.10; the shipped build, two runs)** | **42.8–43.5** (down 41.9–42.2) | **2637–2672** | 153 | **406–407 (85%)** |
104	| … the same build with no C store at all (`STORE_TILES=0`, G3, §2.14: wrong by construction) | 47.1 | **2900** | **130** | 406 (85%): the store costs the pipe nothing, the 9% is clock |
105	| H3's attention, transposed (G4, §3.8, three runs) | 37.3–37.8 (480p), 35.2 (768p) | 2650–2690 / 2600 | 154 | 350–355 (**73%**); the honest floor 81%, with L0 hits 87–90% |
106	
107	Two things this table says that the old one did not. **The GEMM runs 3%
108	under the probe's clock** (2813 against 2899, at 137 W against 110), so
109	the ceiling it should be held to is 53.9, not 55.5, and the gap is 22–25%,
110	not 24–30%. And **the pipeline numbers have no clock behind them**: the

145	TFLOP/s**; the winner won by needing less energy a FLOP under the same
146	cap. So the roofline that binds a real kernel on this part is joules,
147	not clocks, and it is already in `results/*.csv` (the `power_w` column):
148	
149	| what | rate | PPT | energy | above ~20 W idle |
150	|---|---|---|---|---|
151	| matrix pipe, registers only, 16 chains (`peak`) | 55.5 TFLOP/s | 98 W | **567 GFLOP/J** | 1.4 pJ a FLOP |
152	| the same at 4 chains (the old probe) | 55.5 | 112 W | 495 | +14 W of loop issue |
153	| `dot4_int8` / packed fp16 FMA / fp32 FMA | 54 / 25 / 23 T | 118–121 W | 450 / 215 / 189 | |
154	| MALL-resident copy (1–4 MB) | 800 GB/s | 105–136 W | 6–8 GB/J | ~100 pJ a byte |
155	| DRAM stream (≥ 6 MB) | 236 GB/s | 136 W | **1.7 GB/J** | **~490 pJ a byte** |
156	| best suite GEMM | 39.0 TFLOP/s | 137 W | 285 GFLOP/J | |
157	| a video forward, every kernel | 32.5 TFLOP/s | 149 W | 218 GFLOP/J | |
158	| LLM prefill, 8,192 tokens, 24 of 48 layers (`cmd/llm -graph`) | 2,680 tok/s (≈1,340 at 48) | **142 W** at 2713 MHz | ≈ 110 mJ a token at 48 layers | |
159	| LLM decode, 24 of 48 layers (`cmd/llm -gen`) | 63.2 tok/s (≈31.6 at 48) | **91 W** at 2590 MHz | ≈ 2.9 J a token at 48 layers | memory-bound: the bytes, not the clock |
160	
161	A DRAM byte costs the energy of ~340 matrix FLOPs, a MALL byte ~70.
162	The matrix cores at full rate are ~80 W over idle, so **at a 150 W cap a
163	real GEMM has ~50 W for everything else** (bytes at every level, address
164	arithmetic, issue), which is 100 GB/s of DRAM-priced traffic or ~500 GB/s
165	of MALL-priced: a kernel at 55 TFLOP/s and AI 43 moves 1.3 TB/s through
166	the L0/L1, and whether that fits depends on the pJ a byte at *those*
167	levels, which are not measured (G0b). This is also why a
168	register-resident loop "reaches peak at ~90 W" wherever it is claimed:
169	that is the probe, and the other 50–70 W in a real kernel is bytes.
170	
171	**An outside calibration** (2026-09-29): `peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server`
172	claims, for the same model on the same part, prefill at 1,567–1,584 tok/s
173	(8k–32k prompts) and 1,517 at 131k, serial decode 37.6 tok/s at 1.5k and
174	34.1 at 32k, and 46–56 tok/s with a draft head plus prompt lookup, at
175	"about 85 W of sustained package power" and a 2,229 MHz median clock
176	during a 32k prefill. Against ours: prefill 1,213 at 8k and 1,011–1,022
177	at 128k (1.25–1.5x behind) at 142 W (so ~2x the energy a token); serial
178	decode 34.4 at depth 0 and 31.5 at 128k (within 10%) at 91 W (about
179	the same joules a token as their 108–118 W would give); our speculative
180	loop is parked at 0.95x where theirs is 1.35–1.5x. The repository is
181	documentation and a container image, not source ("Shell", no kernel
182	files), so the how is not inspectable. The image was not run here, on
183	purpose: the hardware is the same part under the same ~150 W cap, so
184	their 85 W at 2229 MHz is what their prefill *draws*, not a limit it
185	runs under, and the comparison needs no more than the two power
186	readings. The prefill gap is the one this vertical can act on: a 2x in
187	joules a token at a *lower* clock says their prefill moves far fewer
188	bytes a token through the memory system than ours, which is G5's
189	territory (4-bit weights straight into the matrix cores without the LDS
190	round trip) and G6's (the streaming kernels between the GEMMs).
191	
192	What it changes: an arm that hides latency without moving fewer bytes
193	(a register prefetch) buys the in-wave stall and no clock; an arm that
194	moves fewer bytes a FLOP (LDS sharing across a workgroup's waves, bigger
195	effective tiles, fewer wasted instructions) buys twice. G2's order below
196	is set by that.

198	## Why 76% and not 90%: the hypotheses, each with its measurement
199	
200	Every GEMM lever in the tree so far changed *what* is loaded (intensity,
201	stride, layout, order). None changed *when*, except §2.7, which changed only
202	the scheduling and was worth 2.1x. The remaining gap is most likely
203	scheduling again.
204	
205	- **H1 — the clock.** 3% is already measured (2813 against 2899). Whether
206	  a sustained kernel loses more is §6.4, never run. *Measure*: sysmon over
207	  a 60 s GEMM loop and over one H3 forward, CPU idle and CPU busy (the
208	  server tokenises and decodes audio beside the device). Cheap, and it
209	  fixes the denominator for everything below.
210	- **H2 — latency exposed at the K-tile boundary.** The shipped loop is
211	  `BK_TILES 1`, no hoist: per K tile a wave issues 4 A + 8 B fragment loads
212	  and 32 MMAs, then the next tile's loads. 32 wave64 MMAs are ~1,100 clocks
213	  of matrix-pipe time (8,192 FLOP each at 239 FLOP/clk/SIMD); a fragment
214	  load from L2 or the MALL is several hundred to ~2,000 clocks. Unless the
215	  compiler already issues tile k+1's loads before tile k's MMAs, each wave
216	  stalls once a tile, and with 2–3 waves a SIMD the pipe idles part of the
217	  time. A 20–25% shortfall is exactly the size of one exposed latency per
218	  tile at this occupancy. *Measure*: G1 reads the ISA (where the
219	  `s_waitcnt` sits relative to the `v_wmma` block), then G2 builds the
220	  register-prefetch arm: tile k+1's 12 fragments loaded into a second
221	  register set before tile k's MMAs issue. That is +24 VGPRs; at WN = 8 it
222	  is 264 and spills, so the arm is WM 4 × WN 4 (16 accumulators, 64 VGPRs)
223	  in a 4-wave 128×128 workgroup, or WM 8 × WN 4, and the AI drop (43 → 32)
224	  is part of what is measured. **This is the lever the plan is built
225	  around.** *G2's answer (§2.9): the latency is the cost, but a fragment
226	  is 8 VGPRs (4x replicated at wave64), ACO copies any fragment carried
227	  across the loop's back-edge element by element, and the prefetch that
228	  fits is a whole slab through LDS at wave32: 74 → 80% per clock.*
229	- **H3 — the issue budget.** A wave64 MMA holds the matrix pipe ~34 clocks;
230	  if the loop spends more than ~30 VALU/SALU issue slots per MMA on
231	  address arithmetic, waitcnts and loads, the SIMD is issue-bound, not
232	  latency-bound. *Measure*: instruction count per K tile from the ISA
233	  (§2.3's route: the B-layout finding was an instruction count). If it is
234	  under ~8 non-MMA instructions an MMA, this is not it.
235	- **H4 — the epilogue.** 32 fp32 tiles a wave stored row-major with no
236	  overlap inside the wave: 63 MB of C at M = 4096 × N = 3840, 0.27 ms at
237	  the bus, of a 2.9 ms GEMM. **~9% if nothing overlaps it**, and other
238	  workgroups' MMAs only overlap it if a second workgroup fits on the CU.
239	  *Measure*: the `C_F16` build (halves it; already exists, allowed where
240	  the consumer narrows anyway) against the fp32 store, and a control that
241	  stores one tile of the 32 (the compiler must not be allowed to drop the
242	  MMAs: keep the store conditional on a push constant).
243	- **H5 — the grid tail.** 480 workgroups of 128×256 at the DiT's shape, one
244	  or two resident a CU, so 6–12 rounds; a shape whose last round is a
245	  quarter full loses up to a round. *Measure*: rate against M in steps of
246	  128 rows on one N, K; the tail's size falls out of the sawtooth.
247	- **H6 — L0/L1 traffic.** At 42 TFLOP/s and AI 43 the fragment loads move
248	  ~1 TB/s, above the MALL's 965 GB/s pure read, so the L0/L1 hit rate is
249	  carrying the kernel. The two waves of a workgroup that share an A slab
250	  each load it. LDS staging lost in §2.1 at AI 8–32 on an unhoisted,
251	  untiled kernel; it has not been asked at the current tiling. *Measure*:
252	  only after G2, and only if the prefetch arm lands short of 85%: one LDS
253	  arm on the *tiled* B (a slab is 512 B contiguous tiles, so the staging
254	  is a copy, not a gather). *G2: built, and it is the shipped kernel;
255	  with the staging loads made L0 hits the build reaches 82%, so the memory
256	  system is now ~3 points and the LDS-side schedule ~18 (G-o8).*
257	- **H7 — the accumulator chain.** 32 independent accumulators a K tile;
258	  the MMA latency is hidden. Not it; listed so no one re-tests it.
259	
260	**Attention** (68–70%, and both shipped head-128 builds spill 112–126):
261	
262	- **A1 — the spill.** `T QT2 KTIL4` spills 112 and wins; `T QT2 KTIL2` is
263	  spill-free at 256 and loses 15%; reloading Q each block removes the
264	  spill and loses 11%. Untried: **a head-dimension split** (two passes of
265	  64 channels; the head-64 build is spill-free at 240 and runs 34
266	  TFLOP/s on the VAE), and **wave64** for the transposed kernel (its
267	  element order is wave32's; the probe says what wave64's is, and at wave64

270	- **A2 — the online rescale.** Every key block rescales the 8 O^T
271	  accumulator tiles of a query tile, 8 elements a lane each, plus the
272	  running sum, whether or not the row max moved. FlashAttention-3's lazy

274	  corrects once at the end; exact up to fp32 rounding order. *Measure*:
275	  the screen, and rms against the plain kernel ≤ 1.1e-4 as M11c gated.

292	## Decisions (so future sessions don't relitigate)
293	
294	1. **The ceiling is per clock, and the clock is set by energy.** A
295	   kernel's utilisation is FLOP/clk/CU against the probe's 480, at the
296	   clock sysmon saw *during that kernel*. Every timing this vertical
297	   records carries its sclk and package power (PPT), and every kernel
298	   table carries **GFLOP/J** (or GB/J) beside its rate. The package is
299	   capped near 150 W (§0.6), so rate = cap ÷ energy per operation: a
300	   kernel that spends fewer joules a FLOP runs at a higher clock and is
301	   faster for that reason alone. Power efficiency is not a second
302	   objective here; it is the same one (§0.7).
303	2. **The suite is the ablation instrument; the vertical kernels are where
304	   a winner ships.** `gemm_wmma.comp` + `results/gemm_wmma.csv` stay a
305	   measured artifact of a kernel that does not move under them (the
306	   header in `dit_gemm.comp` says why). A lever is proved in the suite on
307	   the `shapes` family (the models' real M, N, K), then ported to
308	   `dit_gemm.comp` as a `-D` and screened in the verticals with their own
309	   tools: `TestGPUShapes`/`H3_PROFILE` (video), the zimage DiT ladder
310	   (image), `cmd/kevload`, the LLM prefill bench.
311	3. **Bit-identical or the vertical's own gate.** A scheduling change
312	   (prefetch, tile order, epilogue store) makes the same MMAs in the same
313	   order and must be byte-identical (`TestGPUForward` asserts it, as
314	   M11d's split did). A numeric change (lazy rescale, fp16 C) goes through
315	   the consumer's gate (rms ≤ 1.1e-4 on a context; the teacher-forced step
316	   bounds), never a max-abs on a free run.
317	4. **Read the ISA before building the arm.** `cmd/probe` is back; a
318	   hypothesis about scheduling or issue is checked in the disassembly
319	   first, because §2.3 and §6.1 showed that is where the answers were.
320	5. **Wave size and element order are per kernel, probed, with a plain
321	   fallback.** Nothing written against a lane layout ships without
322	   `checkCoopMatLayout`'s equivalent selecting it at first use.
323	6. **A finding is filed under the next free `§N.M`** (§2.9 the prefetch,
324	   §3.8 the attention rescale, §2.10 the register dequant …) with its
325	   file in `research/`, and the G-stage here points at it. Numbers are
326	   never reused.
327	7. **Stop when three consecutive well-formed hypotheses move nothing by
328	   2%.** The exit is a measured plateau, not a percentage: 85% is the
329	   target, not the gate.

The m4 build's 71 allocator moves a step are register pressure at 256 VGPRs (the m2 carries four), and both arms on them are dead: the K tiles as a loop adds 38 moves a tile, A fetched at the top of the step removes the moves for **−12%**. There is no 5% left in the unpack; G5 is closed on this kernel |
343	| G6 | The streaming kernels: a bandwidth column in every vertical's profile, the ones under 200 GB/s listed and fixed or fused (`hc.cn` at 134 first) | |
344	| G7 | The budget: what the server's CPU work beside a device job costs in GPU clock (the audio decode's 32 threads, staging on 32 cores, tokenising; G0 measured 32 busy threads at 1.67x), whether a thread cap or a CPU power limit is a net win, and the sampler folded into `bench/sysmon.go` around the vertical tests | G0 measured the extremes; the server's own load is open |
345	| G8 | Carry-in: each vertical's screen re-run on the new builds, the numbers into VIDEO.md M11, the image and LLM records, and TODO.md's table | continuous. **G2 carried to all nine hosts 2026-09-29** (table below): every gate passes; the image step 2179 → 2058 ms, the VAE decode 37.1 → 35.5 s, Kev's fp16 pass at 494 tokens 154 → 132 ms; **the build loses below ~1000 rows** (a 30-workgroup grid), so `ace/dit` keeps the wave64 build up to 1024 rows and the ladders' schedules already keep it off short inputs |
346	
347	**Order:** G0 (a day: it fixes the denominator), G1 (a session: it decides
348	between H2 and H3 before anything is built), G2 (the big one), then G4 and
349	G5 in either order, G3 and G6 as the profiles point, G7 when a long run is
350	happening anyway, G8 after every win.
351	
352	**Gates, per stage:** G0 a ceiling table reproduced twice with clocks. G1 a
353	written schedule of one K iteration from the disassembly, with the
354	instruction counts. G2 the suite's best and `dit.qkv`'s rate, two runs
355	each, bit-identical C, and the register/spill line from `cmd/probe`. G3
356	the priced store and the sawtooth, both with clocks. G4 the H3 screen
357	table and rms against the plain kernel, plus `TestGPUForward`/`TestGPURun`
358	unchanged. G5 bit-identical to the LDS path on the MoE bench, and the
359	prefill rate. G6 a table of every streaming kernel over 1 ms in a block
360	with its GB/s. G7 the trace.
361	
362	### G0 — instruments and the ceiling (2026-09-29)
363	
364	Filed as **§0.6** in `research/0-measurement-validity.md`.
365	
366	**The ceiling is the hardware's.** The `peak` family gained the WMMA loop
367	at 8 and 16 chains and at wave32 (`-DACC`, `-DWAVE`; `bench/ops_peak.go`
368	pins the size), so G-o1 could be answered instead of assumed:
369	
370	| probe | best | sclk | W | FLOP/clk/CU |
371	|---|---|---|---|---|
372	| wmma_fp16, 4 chains, wave64 (the old probe) | 55,554 | 2890 | 112 | 481 |
373	| 8 chains | 55,615 | 2890 | 99 | 481 |
374	| 16 chains | 55,524 | 2890 | 98 | 480 |
375	| wave32, 4 chains | 55,436 | 2892 | 98 | 479 |
376	| wave32, 8 chains | 55,405 | 2896 | 100 | 478 |
377	| wmma_int8 | 55,538 | 2879 | 98 | 482 |
378	
379	Flat to 1% across all of them, at **480 of the spec's 512**, which is
380	15/16 exactly: the matrix pipe's dense rate on this silicon, not a probe
381	artefact. 55.5 TFLOP/s at 2899 MHz stands, and every rate below is read
382	against 480 FLOP/clk/CU at the clock the kernel ran at.
383	
384	**The clock under a real kernel.** A 100 ms sampler on
385	`hwmon/freq1_input` and `power1_average` around `TestGPUShapes`
386	(`H3_SHAPES=1 H3_PROFILE=1`, int8, the machine otherwise idle):
387	
388	| what | sclk (mode) | package W | a 480p forward | a 768p forward |
389	|---|---|---|---|---|
390	| `peak` probe | 2890–2899 | 100–112 | | |
391	| suite GEMM, 20 ms bursts (`results/gemm_wmma.csv`) | 2813 | 137 | | |
392	| **H3 forward, CPU idle** | **2600–2650** | **149** | 30.0 s | |
393	| H3 768p forward, CPU idle (sustained ~2 min) | 2550–2600 | 142–155 | | 106.7 s |
394	| **H3 forward, 32 busy CPU threads** | **1300–1400** | 121 (GPU side) | **50.1 s** | **190 s** |
395	
396	Three things. **The package is power-limited at ~150 W**, and a GEMM's
397	memory traffic costs ~40 W over the register-only probe, so the clock
398	sags 9–10% under any real kernel: the ceiling during a video forward is
399	**49.9 TFLOP/s**, not 55.5, and the shipped GEMM's 37 TFLOP/s there is
400	**74% per clock** (353 FLOP/clk/CU), the attention's 37.3 is 75%, the
401	whole forward's 32.5 is 65%. **The 768p run sags further** (2550–2600),
402	so long forwards are ~2% slower per FLOP than short ones for the clock
403	alone. And **the CPU shares the budget**: 32 busy host threads halve the
404	GPU clock and make a forward 1.67x slower. That is the mechanism behind
405	VIDEO.md M11f's "+2.4 s of device time while the audio decodes on 32
406	threads": not memory contention, the power budget. Anything the server
407	runs on the CPU beside a device job costs GPU clock in proportion to its
408	power, which is a serving rule this repo did not have.
409	
410	**Instruments.** `cmd/probe` is back (`RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats|asm`),
411	`H3_GEMM_SPV=path` runs a big-GEMM build from disk in `TestGPUShapes`
412	(and times it even when it is wrong by construction), and the sampler
413	is `scratchpad/sample.sh`-shaped: 100 ms of `freq1_input`,
414	`power1_average`; a phase is the samples between two timestamps. It is
415	not in the tree yet; G7 should fold it into `bench/sysmon.go` around the
416	vertical tests.
417	
418	### G1 — the shipped GEMM's schedule (2026-09-29)
419	
420	Filed as **§6.5** in `research/6.5-gemm-schedule.md`.
421	
422	**The loop, from the disassembly** (`dit_gemm_wg128x256_bt16_swz8`,
423	wave64, 240 VGPRs, no spill, no LDS; ACO says 6 subgroups a SIMD, which
424	is not the arithmetic of a 1536-register file at wave64 and is not
425	relied on). One iteration is one 16-wide K tile:
426	
427	| instructions | count | what |
428	|---|---|---|
429	| `v_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16` | 32 | the 4×8 accumulator grid |
430	| `buffer_load_b128` | 24 | 4 A + 8 B fragments, 2 loads each, in 3 clauses |
431	| `s_add/s_mul/s_lshr/s_lshl/s_load/s_mov` | 56 | the B tile addresses, **recomputed every iteration** |
432	| `v_lshlrev/v_add3/v_mul_lo/v_mbcnt/v_and` | 29 | the A addresses and lane offset, likewise |
433	| `s_delay_alu` | 20 | dependency stalls in that arithmetic |
434	| `s_waitcnt` | 9 | `vmcnt(14)`, then 12, 10, … 0, four MMAs between each |
435	| `s_clause`, branch, compare | 5 | |
436	
437	Order: address arithmetic → all 24 loads → `s_waitcnt vmcnt(14)` (A and
438	the first B landed) → 4 MMAs → wait → 4 MMAs … → `vmcnt(0)` → the last 4
439	→ loop. **G-o3 answered: no.** ACO does not hoist the next tile's loads
440	above this tile's MMAs; each iteration pays the load latency once, from
441	the address arithmetic to the tenth load landing, with only the other
442	waves on the SIMD to fill it. 4.5 non-MMA instructions an MMA, so it is
443	not issue-bound by count (H3); but ~85 of them sit on the critical path
444	in front of the loads.
445	
446	**Occupancy does not move it** (`-DLDS_PAD`, an unused shared array that
447	caps workgroups a WGP; `H3_GEMM_SPV`, 480p, int8):
448	
449	| build | LDS | workgroups a CU | gemm qkv | gate / up | o | forward |
450	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
451	| shipped | 0 | ≥ 3 | 36.9 | 36.6 / 36.6 | 34.5 | 30.10 s |
452	| `LDS_PAD=4096` | 16 KB | 4 | 37.2 | 36.7 / 36.6 | 34.1 | 30.21 s |
453	| `LDS_PAD=8192` | 32 KB | 2 | 37.3 | 36.6 / 36.5 | 34.2 | 30.04 s |
454	| `LDS_PAD=16384` | 64 KB | **1** | 37.6 | 37.0 / 36.9 | 34.7 | 30.00 s |
455	
456	Flat to 1%, down to one 4-wave workgroup a CU. So the exposed latency is
457	not being covered by other waves at *any* of these occupancies, and
458	adding waves is not a lever (G-o2 is moot for this kernel).
459	
460	**Take the memory system away** (`-DL0_LOADS=1`: every fragment load
461	reads one of two K tiles, so the 24 loads are issued and waited for as
462	before but every one is an L0 hit; the result is garbage by
463	construction; the `down` projection keeps the shipped KRANGE build, so
464	it is a control):
465	
466	| | shipped, real loads | `L0_LOADS` | |
467	|---|---|---|---|
468	| gemm qkv | 36.9 | **43.6** | 1.18x |
469	| gemm gate / up | 36.6 / 36.6 | **44.2 / 44.0** | 1.21x |
470	| gemm o | 34.5 | **42.8** | 1.24x |
471	| gemm down (control, real loads) | 26.7 | 29.9 | the clock |
472	| attention (unchanged kernel) | 37.2 | 39.4 | the clock |
473	| sclk during the forward | 2600–2650 | 2650–2700 (less memory power) | |
474	| **per clock, FLOP/clk/CU** | **353 (74%)** | **~405 (82–85%)** | |
475	
476	So the gap decomposes: **~10 points are the memory system** (the
477	difference between L0 hits and the real slabs, at the same schedule),
478	and **~16 points are the in-wave schedule** with the loads perfect: the
479	once-a-tile stall from the address arithmetic through the L0 latency to
480	the tenth load, against ~1,090 clocks of MMA. Neither part responds to
481	occupancy, which is what the LDS arms say.
482	
483	**What G2 builds, in order** (re-ranked by the energy roofline, §0.7).
484	(1) Strength-reduce the addresses: every fragment's offset advances by a
485	constant per iteration, so the 85 instructions are 12 adds; cheap,
486	bit-identical, shortens the critical path in front of every iteration's
487	loads, and issue costs watts (the 4-chain probe burns 14 W more than the
488	16-chain one for the same MMAs). (2) Fewer bytes a FLOP: LDS sharing of
489	each slab across the workgroup's 4 waves (the two waves that share an A
490	slab each load it today; H6, untested at this tiling) and the largest
491	per-wave tile the registers allow, measured in TFLOP/s *and* W, because
492	traffic is the power and the power is the clock. (3) Prefetch one K
493	tile ahead into a second register set, so the loads a wave waits on
494	were issued 1,090 clocks earlier: +24 VGPRs, which at WN = 8 means a 4×4
495	or 8×4 grid instead; it buys the in-wave stall and no clock. Bit-identical
496	C for all three, `TestGPUForward`; every arm reports GFLOP/J.
497	
498	**Hypotheses after G0/G1:** H1 confirmed and larger than thought (10%
499	of the ceiling is the clock; G7 asks whether anything can be done about
500	it). H2 alive as the in-wave stall, not as an occupancy story. H3 alive
501	only as the address arithmetic on the critical path. H4, H5 unmeasured.
502	H6 is the ~10 memory points. H7 dead.
503	
504	### G2 — the prefetch that fits (2026-09-29)
505	
506	Filed as **§2.9** in `research/2.9-lds-staged-wave32-gemm.md`, with the
507	whole ladder. The shipped build is now `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` (and
508	`_krange`): eight wave32 waves of 4×4 tiles in the same 128×256
509	workgroup, the K slab (two tiles) fetched by the workgroup as 6 `uvec4`
510	a lane a slab ahead, written to the other of two LDS planes behind the
511	MMAs, one barrier a slab, fragments read from LDS at a conflict-free
512	pitch of 36 halves. Bit-identical to the wave64 build (`H3_GEMM_REF`,
513	`TestGPUForward`).
514	
515	| 480p, int8 | qkv | gate / up | o | down | forward | sclk | per clock |
516	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
517	| wave64 4×8 (was shipped) | 37.2 | 37.3 / 37.1 | 35.4 | 28.7 | 29.86 s | 2620 | 74% |
518	| **`lds_w32`, two runs** | **41.1 / 40.9** | **40.7 / 40.7** | **38.9 / 39.1** | **40.8 / 40.6** | **27.16 / 27.11 s** | 2665 | **80%** |
519	
520	The three findings that decided it: **a wave64 fragment is 8 VGPRs**
521	(4x replicated across the lane groups), so §6.5's "+24 VGPRs" for a
522	prefetched tile was +96 and no register prefetch fits beside a 4×8
523	grid; **ACO copies a fragment carried across a loop back-edge element
524	by element** (200 `v_mov_b16` a trip), so the two register-pipelining
525	arms were dead before they ran, and only a build that carries nothing
526	(a hoisted two-tile slab: +18% at the same intensity; or LDS) measures
527	the idea; and **wave32 and LDS are one lever**: wave32 halves the bytes a
528	fragment read moves but caps the tile at 4×4 and, fed from global memory,
529	runs at 21.5; fed from LDS it runs at 40.9. Refused on the way, all
530	bit-identical: strength-reduced addresses (nothing: the arithmetic was
531	never the cost), four hoisted tiles (no better than two), the read
532	order inside a slab (nothing), LDS pitches of 16 and 24 halves (the
533	reads are `ds_load_b64`, 16 lanes a clock: 4-way and 2-way conflicted).
534	
535	**What is left** (§2.9 item 5): with the staging loads all L0 hits the
536	build reaches 82% per clock, so the global side is ~3 points and the
537	LDS-side schedule (64 `ds_load_b64`, 6 stores, a barrier and the
538	`lgkmcnt` ladder a 544-clock slab) is ~18. G-o8.
539	
540	### G8 — the carry-in (2026-09-29)
541	
542	Every host of the 128×256 kernel now creates `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32`
543	pinned to wave32 (a `wave` field on each variant table; `K % 32` where a
544	host checks its tiles), through its own gate and screen, the same
545	session, the machine otherwise idle:
546	
547	| host | gate | screen, old → new | note |
548	|---|---|---|---|
549	| `h3/dit` | `TestGPUForward`, bit-identical | 480p forward 29.86 → 27.11 s | G2 |
550	| `h3/vae` | `TestGPUDecoder`, PSNR 81.7 dB unchanged | 480p decode 37.1 → **35.5 s** device, 768p 66.1 s | its bias column made K = H + 16; K now rounds to the big GEMM's tile (`gemmVariants[gemmBig].bk`), the pad columns zero in A and B |
551	| `qimage/dit` | `TestGPUOracle1024` | `TestGPUGEMMScreen`, one staging: swz8 2179 → **`lds_w32` 2058 ms a step** (−5.6%; swz2/4/16 +30/+18/+10%) | the fifth arm of the screen, the default |
552	| `ace/dit` | `TestGPUDiT` | 8 forwards at 30 s / 2 / 4 / 10 min: **wave64 0.96** / lds 3.27 (w64 3.24) / **6.76** (6.93) / **18.79** (19.37) s | **the LDS build loses at 375 rows** (130 against 120 ms: 30 workgroups, the barrier shows), ties at 1500, wins 2.5–3% from 3000; `bigW64Rows = 1024` picks the wave64 build below that; the 64×64 rung is 131 / 488 / 1002 / 3215 ms, never the answer |
553	| `kev` (fp16 bank) | `TestGPURowMatchesKev` | `TestGPUGEMMLadder`, 494 tokens: 154.2 → **132.4 ms** (reg64 at 37 tokens 49.7 both days, so the machine is the same) | serves int8 (`q8m4`, 155.3 at 494), which the fp16 rung now beats there: G5's argument |
554	| `parakeet` | `TestGPUEncoderStack` | ladder, `wg128x256`: 138 / 384 / 768 / 1024 frames 28.8 / 36.9 / 67.3 / 111.6 → 31.1 / 40.9 / 66.9 / 109.1 ms | its plan never picks the rung (`reg32x32_w32` wins every clip); at 8–12 workgroups the build loses 8–11% |
555	| `zimage/qwen` | `TestGPUEncoder`, `TestGPUKernelsAgree` | — (its rung is the >192-token one) | rung name now `wg128x256_lds_w32` |
556	| `ocr` | `TestLM`, `TestEngine` (all six cases token-identical) | the page's 1,234-row prefill 100 → 102 ms | the prefill is 2.5% of a page |
557	| `ace/lm` | `TestLogits`, `TestDeterministic` | prefill 239 rows 106 ms | rows ≤ 256 are GEMVs |
558	
559	**The rule it adds:** the LDS-staged build needs the machine full. Its
560	per-slab barrier and staging cost show whenever the grid is under ~40
561	workgroups (rows × N / 32,768), and the hosts whose inputs are short
562	(parakeet, the LM prefills, a 30 s clip) already run smaller rungs or a
563	wave64 build there. Where a host's screen gave a number, it is above.
564	
565	### G5a — the MoE up GEMM's K loop as a pipeline (2026-09-29)
566	
567	Filed as **§2.11** in `research/2.11-moe-gemm-pipeline.md`.
568	
569	**Read the ISA first, then price the parts.** The shipped `up_q4k_m4`
570	(one wave64, a 4×4 tile grid over two 64-column slabs, BK 32) is per
571	K-step four permutation loads, four gathered `uvec4` of A, per slab
572	column a sixteen-byte header and two `uvec4` of nibbles with ~150 VALU
573	of decode, twelve `ds_store_b128`, then 96 `ds_load_b64` and 64 MMAs —
574	256 VGPRs, four subgroups a SIMD, and no barrier at all (one wave). Every
575	load is issued after the previous step's MMAs and waited for before this
576	step's; every bank load is sixty-four lanes at sixty-four rows 1440 B
577	apart, sixteen bytes used of each line, and the same lines again next
578	step. The controls (`-D` knobs, wrong by construction, loaded with the
579	new `LLM_MOE_SPV` into `cmd/llm -moe -tokens 2048`, the m4 rung, layer 3,
580	the real routing):
581	
582	| taken away | `moe.up` | vs 11.53 ms |
583	|---|---:|---:|
584	| the A gather's fetch (`MOE_L0_A`) / the A staging (`MOE_NO_ASTAGE`) | 10.53 / 10.48 | 1.09x / 1.10x |
585	| the bank's fetch, same sixty-four lines a load (`MOE_L0_BANK=2`) | 8.81 | **1.31x** |
586	| the scale path (`MOE_NIB_ONLY`, P12-3) | 8.43 | 1.37x |
587	| the bank's fetch and its divergence (`MOE_L0_BANK=1`) | 8.02 | **1.44x** |
588	| the B unpack (`MOE_NO_UNPACK`) | 6.56 | 1.76x |
589	| both stagings: MMAs and fragment reads alone | 5.33 | 2.16x (47.8 TFLOP/s, the pipe at that clock) |
590	| (added) every fragment read twice (`MOE_FRAG2`) | 12.51 | 0.92x |
591	
592	So the LDS round trip §2.2 blamed is ~8 points, and the bank's fetch —
593	latency in front of every step plus the re-reading of lines — is 25–30.
594	G5's register-built fragment would replicate the unpack 4x at wave64 to
595	save those 8; not built.
596	
597	**The arm** (`-DPIPE=2` on `llm_moe_gemm.comp`, the Q4_K up mode): the
598	bytes a lane unpacks at step k+1 are fetched into registers before step
599	k's MMAs, the permutation entries once before the loop, **the header
600	once a super-block and the nibble group once per two steps** (9 bank
601	loads a super-block instead of 24); the unpack, slabs and fragment reads
602	are the shipped ones, so the MMAs see the same halves in the same order.
603	Bit-identical (`TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` on each of the seven geometries,
604	the whole `TestMoEGPU*` suite with all seven loaded):
605	
606	| `moe.up`, µs a layer | 512 (m2) | 2048 (m4) | 4096 (m4) |
607	|---|---:|---:|---:|
608	| shipped | 6 508 | 11 512 | 17 106 |
609	| a step ahead, every load every step (`PIPE=1`) | 6 185 | 11 054 | 15 008 |
610	| **… and each block's bytes once (`PIPE=2`, shipped)** | **3 241 (2.01x)** | **6 837 (1.68x)** | **10 925 (1.57x)** |
611	
612	Executed 22.1 → 37.3 TFLOP/s at 2048 (~75% per clock; useful 11.7 →
613	19.6 under the m4 rung's 1.90x padding). `PIPE=1` alone is 4–14%
614	because the allocator copies the fetched registers inside the MMA block
615	and waits there (§2.10's moves again); a two-set form spills at m4 and
616	buys nothing where it fits. Refused: the wave32 m4 (spills 217), the
617	two-set pipeline, the register fragment. The seven `llm_moe_up_q4k_*`
618	generate lines carry `-DPIPE=2`; every other build keeps the plain loop.
619	
620	**In the whole model** (`cmd/llm -graph -tokens 2048,4096,8192 -ctx 8192`,
621	48 layers, the shipped banks, old and new binaries interleaved twice the
622	same hour): prefill **1194 / 1206 → 1407 / 1408 tok/s at 2048 (1.17x)**,
623	1317 / 1339 → 1494 / 1495 at 4096 (1.13x), 1306 / 1345 → 1459 / 1462 at
624	8192 (1.10x); the embedded builds pass the whole `TestMoEGPU*` suite and
625	the 1024-token ladder keeps `moeGEMMPlanFor`'s m2/m4 boundary.
626	
627	**The down mode, the same session (G5b):** the pipeline written for the
628	block-32 down formats (B only; twenty builds, all spill-free, the whole
629	suite passing) moves **Q5_1 by nothing** (6 587 → 6 607 µs at 2048,
630	though its `L0_BANK` control read 1.29x: that control removed the load's
631	own cost, not latency, and a 32-element block a step has nothing to
632	hoist) and **IQ4_NL, the served down format, by 1.05x at 2048, 1.20x at
633	512, 1.04x at 4096** (5 634 → 5 366; 2 718 → 2 266; 8 264 → 7 946), which
634	is its nine-word pair read once per two steps. The five IQ4_NL down
635	builds ship with `-DPIPE=2` (embedded, the suite passing; whole-model
636	prefill 1408 → 1422 tok/s at 2048 and 1502 → 1507 at 4096, two runs
637	each); Q5_1, Q4_1 and Q8_0 keep the plain loop.
638	What binds the down mode now is its A fragment loads inside the MMA
639	block, which a fragment's back-edge copy (§2.9) keeps from pipelining.

# KERNELS — the matrix cores to their ceiling

> **Live tracking and session handoff doc, opened 2026-09-29.** Stage
> letters are **G** (GEMM; K is classification, W and R are speech). This
> is the project's first vertical, reopened: not a model, but the kernels
> every vertical stands on. A closed finding still gets a `§N.M` number and
> a file in `research/` as before (README there: the number is the address,
> never renumber); the G-stage here is where it is tracked while open. When
> the vertical closes, this file is frozen to `research/kernels-vertical.md`.

## What we are building

`GOALS.md`'s first sentence: *the most efficient ways to run these models
on Vulkan on this part*. Every vertical since has been a model brought up
on the kernels this one produced, and each of them ended on the same
sentence: "the GEMMs are at their ceiling, the bigger fish is elsewhere".
That ceiling was **42.0 TFLOP/s against a measured 55.5**, and it has not
moved since stage 4 (2026-09-21). Eight verticals later, the matrix cores
are the one place where a win lands in *every* served request at once: a
480p video forward is 63% GEMM and 33% attention on these kernels, an
image step 72% GEMM, a prefill chunk mostly GEMM. **A 1.15x on the GEMM is
worth more than any single vertical's remaining backlog.**

The deliverable is three kernel classes at a higher fraction of the
per-clock ceiling than today, carried into the verticals through the

## The energy roofline (2026-09-29, §0.7)

The GEMM ladder at N = 2048 drew **136–137 W at every rung from 23 to 39
TFLOP/s**; the winner won by needing less energy a FLOP under the same
cap. So the roofline that binds a real kernel on this part is joules,
not clocks, and it is already in `results/*.csv` (the `power_w` column):

| what | rate | PPT | energy | above ~20 W idle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| matrix pipe, registers only, 16 chains (`peak`) | 55.5 TFLOP/s | 98 W | **567 GFLOP/J** | 1.4 pJ a FLOP |
| the same at 4 chains (the old probe) | 55.5 | 112 W | 495 | +14 W of loop issue |
| `dot4_int8` / packed fp16 FMA / fp32 FMA | 54 / 25 / 23 T | 118–121 W | 450 / 215 / 189 | |
| MALL-resident copy (1–4 MB) | 800 GB/s | 105–136 W | 6–8 GB/J | ~100 pJ a byte |
| DRAM stream (≥ 6 MB) | 236 GB/s | 136 W | **1.7 GB/J** | **~490 pJ a byte** |
| best suite GEMM | 39.0 TFLOP/s | 137 W | 285 GFLOP/J | |
| a video forward, every kernel | 32.5 TFLOP/s | 149 W | 218 GFLOP/J | |
| LLM prefill, 8,192 tokens, 24 of 48 layers (`cmd/llm -graph`) | 2,680 tok/s (≈1,340 at 48) | **142 W** at 2713 MHz | ≈ 110 mJ a token at 48 layers | |
| LLM decode, 24 of 48 layers (`cmd/llm -gen`) | 63.2 tok/s (≈31.6 at 48) | **91 W** at 2590 MHz | ≈ 2.9 J a token at 48 layers | memory-bound: the bytes, not the clock |

A DRAM byte costs the energy of ~340 matrix FLOPs, a MALL byte ~70.
The matrix cores at full rate are ~80 W over idle, so **at a 150 W cap a
real GEMM has ~50 W for everything else** (bytes at every level, address
arithmetic, issue), which is 100 GB/s of DRAM-priced traffic or ~500 GB/s
of MALL-priced: a kernel at 55 TFLOP/s and AI 43 moves 1.3 TB/s through
the L0/L1, and whether that fits depends on the pJ a byte at *those*
levels, which are not measured (G0b). This is also why a
register-resident loop "reaches peak at ~90 W" wherever it is claimed:
that is the probe, and the other 50–70 W in a real kernel is bytes.

**An outside calibration** (2026-09-29): `peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server`
claims, for the same model on the same part, prefill at 1,567–1,584 tok/s
(8k–32k prompts) and 1,517 at 131k, serial decode 37.6 tok/s at 1.5k and
34.1 at 32k, and 46–56 tok/s with a draft head plus prompt lookup, at
"about 85 W of sustained package power" and a 2,229 MHz median clock
during a 32k prefill. Against ours: prefill 1,213 at 8k and 1,011–1,022
at 128k (1.25–1.5x behind) at 142 W (so ~2x the energy a token); serial
decode 34.4 at depth 0 and 31.5 at 128k (within 10%) at 91 W (about
the same joules a token as their 108–118 W would give); our speculative
loop is parked at 0.95x where theirs is 1.35–1.5x. The repository is
documentation and a container image, not source ("Shell", no kernel
files), so the how is not inspectable. The image was not run here, on
purpose: the hardware is the same part under the same ~150 W cap, so
their 85 W at 2229 MHz is what their prefill *draws*, not a limit it
runs under, and the comparison needs no more than the two power
readings. The prefill gap is the one this vertical can act on: a 2x in
joules a token at a *lower* clock says their prefill moves far fewer
bytes a token through the memory system than ours, which is G5's
territory (4-bit weights straight into the matrix cores without the LDS
round trip) and G6's (the streaming kernels between the GEMMs).

What it changes: an arm that hides latency without moving fewer bytes
(a register prefetch) buys the in-wave stall and no clock; an arm that
moves fewer bytes a FLOP (LDS sharing across a workgroup's waves, bigger
effective tiles, fewer wasted instructions) buys twice. G2's order below
is set by that.

## Why 76% and not 90%: the hypotheses, each with its measurement

Every GEMM lever in the tree so far changed *what* is loaded (intensity,
stride, layout, order). None changed *when*, except §2.7, which changed only
the scheduling and was worth 2.1x. The remaining gap is most likely
scheduling again.

- **H1 — the clock.** 3% is already measured (2813 against 2899). Whether
  a sustained kernel loses more is §6.4, never run. *Measure*: sysmon over
  a 60 s GEMM loop and over one H3 forward, CPU idle and CPU busy (the
  server tokenises and decodes audio beside the device). Cheap, and it
  fixes the denominator for everything below.
- **H2 — latency exposed at the K-tile boundary.** The shipped loop is
  `BK_TILES 1`, no hoist: per K tile a wave issues 4 A + 8 B fragment loads
  and 32 MMAs, then the next tile's loads. 32 wave64 MMAs are ~1,100 clocks
  of matrix-pipe time (8,192 FLOP each at 239 FLOP/clk/SIMD); a fragment
  load from L2 or the MALL is several hundred to ~2,000 clocks. Unless the
  compiler already issues tile k+1's loads before tile k's MMAs, each wave
  stalls once a tile, and with 2–3 waves a SIMD the pipe idles part of the
  time. A 20–25% shortfall is exactly the size of one exposed latency per
  tile at this occupancy. *Measure*: G1 reads the ISA (where the
  `s_waitcnt` sits relative to the `v_wmma` block), then G2 builds the
  register-prefetch arm: tile k+1's 12 fragments loaded into a second
  register set before tile k's MMAs issue. That is +24 VGPRs; at WN = 8 it
  is 264 and spills, so the arm is WM 4 × WN 4 (16 accumulators, 64 VGPRs)
  in a 4-wave 128×128 workgroup, or WM 8 × WN 4, and the AI drop (43 → 32)
  is part of what is measured. **This is the lever the plan is built
  around.** *G2's answer (§2.9): the latency is the cost, but a fragment
  is 8 VGPRs (4x replicated at wave64), ACO copies any fragment carried
  across the loop's back-edge element by element, and the prefetch that
  fits is a whole slab through LDS at wave32: 74 → 80% per clock.*
- **H3 — the issue budget.** A wave64 MMA holds the matrix pipe ~34 clocks;
  if the loop spends more than ~30 VALU/SALU issue slots per MMA on
  address arithmetic, waitcnts and loads, the SIMD is issue-bound, not
  latency-bound. *Measure*: instruction count per K tile from the ISA
  (§2.3's route: the B-layout finding was an instruction count). If it is
  under ~8 non-MMA instructions an MMA, this is not it.
- **H4 — the epilogue.** 32 fp32 tiles a wave stored row-major with no
  overlap inside the wave: 63 MB of C at M = 4096 × N = 3840, 0.27 ms at
  the bus, of a 2.9 ms GEMM. **~9% if nothing overlaps it**, and other
  workgroups' MMAs only overlap it if a second workgroup fits on the CU.
  *Measure*: the `C_F16` build (halves it; already exists, allowed where
  the consumer narrows anyway) against the fp32 store, and a control that
  stores one tile of the 32 (the compiler must not be allowed to drop the
  MMAs: keep the store conditional on a push constant).
- **H5 — the grid tail.** 480 workgroups of 128×256 at the DiT's shape, one
  or two resident a CU, so 6–12 rounds; a shape whose last round is a
  quarter full loses up to a round. *Measure*: rate against M in steps of
  128 rows on one N, K; the tail's size falls out of the sawtooth.
- **H6 — L0/L1 traffic.** At 42 TFLOP/s and AI 43 the fragment loads move
  ~1 TB/s, above the MALL's 965 GB/s pure read, so the L0/L1 hit rate is
  carrying the kernel. The two waves of a workgroup that share an A slab
  each load it. LDS staging lost in §2.1 at AI 8–32 on an unhoisted,
  untiled kernel; it has not been asked at the current tiling. *Measure*:
  only after G2, and only if the prefetch arm lands short of 85%: one LDS
  arm on the *tiled* B (a slab is 512 B contiguous tiles, so the staging
  is a copy, not a gather). *G2: built, and it is the shipped kernel;
  with the staging loads made L0 hits the build reaches 82%, so the memory
  system is now ~3 points and the LDS-side schedule ~18 (G-o8).*
- **H7 — the accumulator chain.** 32 independent accumulators a K tile;
  the MMA latency is hidden. Not it; listed so no one re-tests it.

**Attention** (68–70%, and both shipped head-128 builds spill 112–126):

- **A1 — the spill.** `T QT2 KTIL4` spills 112 and wins; `T QT2 KTIL2` is
  spill-free at 256 and loses 15%; reloading Q each block removes the
  spill and loses 11%. Untried: **a head-dimension split** (two passes of
  64 channels; the head-64 build is spill-free at 240 and runs 34
  TFLOP/s on the VAE), and **wave64** for the transposed kernel (its
  element order is wave32's; the probe says what wave64's is, and at wave64
  the same tile needs half the VGPRs per fragment). *Measure*: the existing
  screen (`TestGPUAttentionScreen`, `H3_ATTN_SPV=qt:ktil:path`).
- **A2 — the online rescale.** Every key block rescales the 8 O^T
  accumulator tiles of a query tile, 8 elements a lane each, plus the
  running sum, whether or not the row max moved. FlashAttention-3's lazy
  rescaling skips it while the max grows by less than a threshold and
  corrects once at the end; exact up to fp32 rounding order. *Measure*:
  the screen, and rms against the plain kernel ≤ 1.1e-4 as M11c gated.
- **A3 — an honest gutting.** M11c's "no LDS round trip" arm read 65.7
  TFLOP/s, above the ceiling, so the compiler dropped MMAs and that arm is
  not a measurement. *Redo*: each phase removed with its result kept live
  (folded into the stored O), so the MMA-only floor of the transposed loop
  is a real number. If it is ~40, the softmax is not the cost and A1 is
  the whole story; if 45+, A2 is worth up to 15%.

**Int8 and Q4 weights** (the LLM's prefill, Kev, embeddings, video's
dequant pass): **G5** builds the B fragment in registers from the bytes
the lane loads itself, using the element order the probe pins (A: lane l
holds row l%16, element e is column e; B: lane l holds column l%16,
element e is row e). No LDS, no barrier, and the plain path stays as the
fallback the probe selects. The MoE Q4 GEMM's 51% is the first customer;
the LLM's prefill graph runs at 9.8 TFLOP/s of useful work (P11), most of
it on these kernels.

## Decisions (so future sessions don't relitigate)

1. **The ceiling is per clock, and the clock is set by energy.** A
   kernel's utilisation is FLOP/clk/CU against the probe's 480, at the
   clock sysmon saw *during that kernel*. Every timing this vertical
   records carries its sclk and package power (PPT), and every kernel
   table carries **GFLOP/J** (or GB/J) beside its rate. The package is
   capped near 150 W (§0.6), so rate = cap ÷ energy per operation: a
   kernel that spends fewer joules a FLOP runs at a higher clock and is
   faster for that reason alone. Power efficiency is not a second
   objective here; it is the same one (§0.7).
2. **The suite is the ablation instrument; the vertical kernels are where
   a winner ships.** `gemm_wmma.comp` + `results/gemm_wmma.csv` stay a
   measured artifact of a kernel that does not move under them (the
   header in `dit_gemm.comp` says why). A lever is proved in the suite on
   the `shapes` family (the models' real M, N, K), then ported to
   `dit_gemm.comp` as a `-D` and screened in the verticals with their own
   tools: `TestGPUShapes`/`H3_PROFILE` (video), the zimage DiT ladder
   (image), `cmd/kevload`, the LLM prefill bench.
3. **Bit-identical or the vertical's own gate.** A scheduling change
   (prefetch, tile order, epilogue store) makes the same MMAs in the same
   order and must be byte-identical (`TestGPUForward` asserts it, as
   M11d's split did). A numeric change (lazy rescale, fp16 C) goes through
   the consumer's gate (rms ≤ 1.1e-4 on a context; the teacher-forced step
   bounds), never a max-abs on a free run.
4. **Read the ISA before building the arm.** `cmd/probe` is back; a
   hypothesis about scheduling or issue is checked in the disassembly
   first, because §2.3 and §6.1 showed that is where the answers were.
5. **Wave size and element order are per kernel, probed, with a plain
   fallback.** Nothing written against a lane layout ships without
   `checkCoopMatLayout`'s equivalent selecting it at first use.
6. **A finding is filed under the next free `§N.M`** (§2.9 the prefetch,
   §3.8 the attention rescale, §2.10 the register dequant …) with its
   file in `research/`, and the G-stage here points at it. Numbers are
   never reused.
7. **Stop when three consecutive well-formed hypotheses move nothing by
   2%.** The exit is a measured plateau, not a percentage: 85% is the
   target, not the gate.

### G0 — instruments and the ceiling (2026-09-29)

Filed as **§0.6** in `research/0-measurement-validity.md`.

**The ceiling is the hardware's.** The `peak` family gained the WMMA loop
at 8 and 16 chains and at wave32 (`-DACC`, `-DWAVE`; `bench/ops_peak.go`
pins the size), so G-o1 could be answered instead of assumed:

| probe | best | sclk | W | FLOP/clk/CU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wmma_fp16, 4 chains, wave64 (the old probe) | 55,554 | 2890 | 112 | 481 |
| 8 chains | 55,615 | 2890 | 99 | 481 |
| 16 chains | 55,524 | 2890 | 98 | 480 |
| wave32, 4 chains | 55,436 | 2892 | 98 | 479 |
| wave32, 8 chains | 55,405 | 2896 | 100 | 478 |
| wmma_int8 | 55,538 | 2879 | 98 | 482 |

Flat to 1% across all of them, at **480 of the spec's 512**, which is
15/16 exactly: the matrix pipe's dense rate on this silicon, not a probe
artefact. 55.5 TFLOP/s at 2899 MHz stands, and every rate below is read
against 480 FLOP/clk/CU at the clock the kernel ran at.

**The clock under a real kernel.** A 100 ms sampler on
`hwmon/freq1_input` and `power1_average` around `TestGPUShapes`
(`H3_SHAPES=1 H3_PROFILE=1`, int8, the machine otherwise idle):

| what | sclk (mode) | package W | a 480p forward | a 768p forward |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `peak` probe | 2890–2899 | 100–112 | | |
| suite GEMM, 20 ms bursts (`results/gemm_wmma.csv`) | 2813 | 137 | | |
| **H3 forward, CPU idle** | **2600–2650** | **149** | 30.0 s | |
| H3 768p forward, CPU idle (sustained ~2 min) | 2550–2600 | 142–155 | | 106.7 s |
| **H3 forward, 32 busy CPU threads** | **1300–1400** | 121 (GPU side) | **50.1 s** | **190 s** |

Three things. **The package is power-limited at ~150 W**, and a GEMM's
memory traffic costs ~40 W over the register-only probe, so the clock
sags 9–10% under any real kernel: the ceiling during a video forward is
**49.9 TFLOP/s**, not 55.5, and the shipped GEMM's 37 TFLOP/s there is
**74% per clock** (353 FLOP/clk/CU), the attention's 37.3 is 75%, the
whole forward's 32.5 is 65%. **The 768p run sags further** (2550–2600),
so long forwards are ~2% slower per FLOP than short ones for the clock
alone. And **the CPU shares the budget**: 32 busy host threads halve the
GPU clock and make a forward 1.67x slower. That is the mechanism behind
VIDEO.md M11f's "+2.4 s of device time while the audio decodes on 32
threads": not memory contention, the power budget. Anything the server
runs on the CPU beside a device job costs GPU clock in proportion to its
power, which is a serving rule this repo did not have.

**Instruments.** `cmd/probe` is back (`RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats|asm`),

### G1 — the shipped GEMM's schedule (2026-09-29)

Filed as **§6.5** in `research/6.5-gemm-schedule.md`.

**The loop, from the disassembly** (`dit_gemm_wg128x256_bt16_swz8`,
wave64, 240 VGPRs, no spill, no LDS; ACO says 6 subgroups a SIMD, which
is not the arithmetic of a 1536-register file at wave64 and is not
relied on). One iteration is one 16-wide K tile:

| instructions | count | what |
|---|---|---|
| `v_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16` | 32 | the 4×8 accumulator grid |
| `buffer_load_b128` | 24 | 4 A + 8 B fragments, 2 loads each, in 3 clauses |
| `s_add/s_mul/s_lshr/s_lshl/s_load/s_mov` | 56 | the B tile addresses, **recomputed every iteration** |
| `v_lshlrev/v_add3/v_mul_lo/v_mbcnt/v_and` | 29 | the A addresses and lane offset, likewise |
| `s_delay_alu` | 20 | dependency stalls in that arithmetic |
| `s_waitcnt` | 9 | `vmcnt(14)`, then 12, 10, … 0, four MMAs between each |
| `s_clause`, branch, compare | 5 | |

Order: address arithmetic → all 24 loads → `s_waitcnt vmcnt(14)` (A and
the first B landed) → 4 MMAs → wait → 4 MMAs … → `vmcnt(0)` → the last 4
→ loop. **G-o3 answered: no.** ACO does not hoist the next tile's loads
above this tile's MMAs; each iteration pays the load latency once, from
the address arithmetic to the tenth load landing, with only the other
waves on the SIMD to fill it. 4.5 non-MMA instructions an MMA, so it is
not issue-bound by count (H3); but ~85 of them sit on the critical path
in front of the loads.

**Occupancy does not move it** (`-DLDS_PAD`, an unused shared array that
caps workgroups a WGP; `H3_GEMM_SPV`, 480p, int8):

| build | LDS | workgroups a CU | gemm qkv | gate / up | o | forward |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped | 0 | ≥ 3 | 36.9 | 36.6 / 36.6 | 34.5 | 30.10 s |
| `LDS_PAD=4096` | 16 KB | 4 | 37.2 | 36.7 / 36.6 | 34.1 | 30.21 s |
| `LDS_PAD=8192` | 32 KB | 2 | 37.3 | 36.6 / 36.5 | 34.2 | 30.04 s |
| `LDS_PAD=16384` | 64 KB | **1** | 37.6 | 37.0 / 36.9 | 34.7 | 30.00 s |

Flat to 1%, down to one 4-wave workgroup a CU. So the exposed latency is
not being covered by other waves at *any* of these occupancies, and
adding waves is not a lever (G-o2 is moot for this kernel).

**Take the memory system away** (`-DL0_LOADS=1`: every fragment load
reads one of two K tiles, so the 24 loads are issued and waited for as
before but every one is an L0 hit; the result is garbage by
construction; the `down` projection keeps the shipped KRANGE build, so
it is a control):

| | shipped, real loads | `L0_LOADS` | |
|---|---|---|---|
| gemm qkv | 36.9 | **43.6** | 1.18x |
| gemm gate / up | 36.6 / 36.6 | **44.2 / 44.0** | 1.21x |
| gemm o | 34.5 | **42.8** | 1.24x |
| gemm down (control, real loads) | 26.7 | 29.9 | the clock |
| attention (unchanged kernel) | 37.2 | 39.4 | the clock |
| sclk during the forward | 2600–2650 | 2650–2700 (less memory power) | |
| **per clock, FLOP/clk/CU** | **353 (74%)** | **~405 (82–85%)** | |

So the gap decomposes: **~10 points are the memory system** (the
difference between L0 hits and the real slabs, at the same schedule),
and **~16 points are the in-wave schedule** with the loads perfect: the
once-a-tile stall from the address arithmetic through the L0 latency to
the tenth load, against ~1,090 clocks of MMA. Neither part responds to
occupancy, which is what the LDS arms say.

**What G2 builds, in order** (re-ranked by the energy roofline, §0.7).
(1) Strength-reduce the addresses: every fragment's offset advances by a
constant per iteration, so the 85 instructions are 12 adds; cheap,
bit-identical, shortens the critical path in front of every iteration's
loads, and issue costs watts (the 4-chain probe burns 14 W more than the
16-chain one for the same MMAs). (2) Fewer bytes a FLOP: LDS sharing of
each slab across the workgroup's 4 waves (the two waves that share an A
slab each load it today; H6, untested at this tiling) and the largest
per-wave tile the registers allow, measured in TFLOP/s *and* W, because
traffic is the power and the power is the clock. (3) Prefetch one K
tile ahead into a second register set, so the loads a wave waits on
were issued 1,090 clocks earlier: +24 VGPRs, which at WN = 8 means a 4×4
or 8×4 grid instead; it buys the in-wave stall and no clock. Bit-identical
C for all three, `TestGPUForward`; every arm reports GFLOP/J.

**Hypotheses after G0/G1:** H1 confirmed and larger than thought (10%
of the ceiling is the clock; G7 asks whether anything can be done about
it). H2 alive as the in-wave stall, not as an occupancy story. H3 alive
only as the address arithmetic on the critical path. H4, H5 unmeasured.
H6 is the ~10 memory points. H7 dead.

### G5a — the MoE up GEMM's K loop as a pipeline (2026-09-29)

Filed as **§2.11** in `research/2.11-moe-gemm-pipeline.md`.

**Read the ISA first, then price the parts.** The shipped `up_q4k_m4`
(one wave64, a 4×4 tile grid over two 64-column slabs, BK 32) is per
K-step four permutation loads, four gathered `uvec4` of A, per slab
column a sixteen-byte header and two `uvec4` of nibbles with ~150 VALU
of decode, twelve `ds_store_b128`, then 96 `ds_load_b64` and 64 MMAs —
256 VGPRs, four subgroups a SIMD, and no barrier at all (one wave). Every
load is issued after the previous step's MMAs and waited for before this
step's; every bank load is sixty-four lanes at sixty-four rows 1440 B
apart, sixteen bytes used of each line, and the same lines again next
step. The controls (`-D` knobs, wrong by construction, loaded with the
new `LLM_MOE_SPV` into `cmd/llm -moe -tokens 2048`, the m4 rung, layer 3,
the real routing):

| taken away | `moe.up` | vs 11.53 ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| the A gather's fetch (`MOE_L0_A`) / the A staging (`MOE_NO_ASTAGE`) | 10.53 / 10.48 | 1.09x / 1.10x |
| the bank's fetch, same sixty-four lines a load (`MOE_L0_BANK=2`) | 8.81 | **1.31x** |
| the scale path (`MOE_NIB_ONLY`, P12-3) | 8.43 | 1.37x |
| the bank's fetch and its divergence (`MOE_L0_BANK=1`) | 8.02 | **1.44x** |
| the B unpack (`MOE_NO_UNPACK`) | 6.56 | 1.76x |
| both stagings: MMAs and fragment reads alone | 5.33 | 2.16x (47.8 TFLOP/s, the pipe at that clock) |
| (added) every fragment read twice (`MOE_FRAG2`) | 12.51 | 0.92x |

So the LDS round trip §2.2 blamed is ~8 points, and the bank's fetch —
latency in front of every step plus the re-reading of lines — is 25–30.
G5's register-built fragment would replicate the unpack 4x at wave64 to
save those 8; not built.

**The arm** (`-DPIPE=2` on `llm_moe_gemm.comp`, the Q4_K up mode): the
bytes a lane unpacks at step k+1 are fetched into registers before step
k's MMAs, the permutation entries once before the loop, **the header
once a super-block and the nibble group once per two steps** (9 bank
loads a super-block instead of 24); the unpack, slabs and fragment reads
are the shipped ones, so the MMAs see the same halves in the same order.
