**Next in G5:** ~~the up rung's padding factor (1.90x executed rows at
m4, 2048 tokens: the largest term left in the up kernel)~~ (G5c), the
Q5_K up build (layer 2), and the down mode's A side.

### G5c — the short last tile (2026-09-30)

Filed as **§2.12** in `research/2.12-moe-short-tiles.md`.

**The rows were the cost now.** P11-4 padded to the fragment three ways
and lost every time because the slab unpack was the kernel; after §2.11
the MMAs are ~78% of it. The permutation's record already said how many
of a block's rows are real (C5 wrote it for the decode GEMV); the
single-wave builds of `llm_moe_gemm.comp` are now `SHORT` builds that
round it to the schedule's alignment (`pc.gemmM`) and run one of WM
copies of the K loop and store on a uniform `switch` — no bound inside
the unrolled loops, the same MMAs per real row in the same order —
and the alignment (`MoEGPU.pad`, `moeAlign`) is sixteen rows unless a
plan names a multi-wave rung. Bit-identical: `TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` at
`maxAbs == 0` across every mixed plan, `TestMoEGPUPaddingIsInert`, and
`TestGraphLogits`'s whole-model line reproduced to the digit against the
old test binary.

| 2048 tokens, m4, µs a layer (old / new, two interleaved runs) | rows | `moe.up` | `moe.down` | block |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| the padded schedule | 1.90x | 6 994 / 7 029 | 6 577 / 6 609 (Q5_1) | 15 733 / 15 793 |
| **SHORT** | **1.19x** (up executes 1.41x) | **6 314 / 6 255** | **5 370 / 5 339** | **13 822 / 13 721** |
| … with the served IQ4_NL down | | 6 922 → 6 374 | 5 373 → **4 209** | 14 441 → **12 727** |

**What decided the form.** Any third copy of the Q4_K up loop spills
11–15 registers its epilogue needs across the K loop, and a control run
of the four-copy build with `LLM_MOE_PAD=64` (every block whole) is 9%
slower than the shipped kernel on the same work; the two-copy form
(`SHORT_STEP=2`: 2 and 4 tiles, the store still bounded by the real
count — the first cut stored the rounded tile over the next expert's
rows, a race the ladder test caught) costs nothing on full blocks and
executes a 16-row tail as 32. The down builds have 120–144 registers and
keep all four. **A short tile's rows are cheap rows**: on the four-copy
build the alignment 64 → 16 sheds 14 608 rows for 1 255 µs, 0.086 µs a
row against the MMA-only control's 0.137, because the tile still unpacks
two whole slabs (~300 VALU a lane a step, a matrix clock each, §2.10)
beside its sixteen MMAs. That unpack is now the largest term in the up
projection at every rung.

**In the whole model** (`cmd/llm -graph`, old and new interleaved twice):
**1416.5 / 1418.6 → 1514.0 / 1513.2 tok/s at 2048 (1.07x)**, 1499.7 /
1502.1 → 1549.4 / 1542.8 at 4096, 1461.4 / 1466.7 → 1480.8 / 1482.7 at
8192. The rung ladder on the SHORT builds puts `m4/m4` ahead of `m2/m2`
from 512 tokens (6 380 against 6 460; 8 999 against 9 361 at 1024) and
behind it at 64–128, so `moeGEMMPlanFor`'s boundary is 256, not 1024.
Tools: `-DSHORT`, `-DSHORT_STEP` on `llm_moe_gemm.comp`, `LLM_MOE_PAD` on
the host (a pre-§2.12 build loaded through `LLM_MOE_SPV` needs it at 64).

### G5d — the nibble as an f16 denormal (2026-09-30)

Filed as **§2.13** in `research/2.13-moe-nibble-denormal.md`.

**The estimate was wrong by the compiler.** §2.12 priced the slab unpack
at ~300 VALU a lane a step and G5's plan was `v_perm`/`v_cvt_pk`
sequences. The ISA of the shipped `up_q4k_m4` says an element is three
instructions, not five — ACO already fuses `ds * nib - dm` and the
`float16_t()` into one `v_fma_mixlo/hi_f16` — so the only work in front
of the floor is a `v_bfe_u32` and a `v_cvt_f32_u32` an element. Both go
by reading the nibble as a half: a halfword whose low nibble is the
value and whose other bits are zero is the f16 denormal `nib × 2^-24`,
`v_fma_mix` takes a half from either half of a word through op_sel, and
`d × sc × 2^24` is as exact as `d × sc`. Three instructions for four
elements, the same fma operands to the bit, and the slab is byte-identical
(`TestMoEGPULadderAgrees` at `maxAbs == 0` with the new m4 against the
old m2/m2; the negative control through the same override fails).

| four-tile K-step, VALU beside 64 MMAs | shipped | `NIB_F16` |
|---|---:|---:|
| extract + convert | 128 | 0 |
| masks | — | 48 |
| `v_fma_mix` (floor) | 64 | 64 |

## How to run

- The suite: `go run ./cmd/bench -h`; families `peak`, `gemm_wmma`,
  `shapes`, `stride`, `moe`, `bank`. Results append to `results/*.csv`
  with sclk and power columns; the harness warms the clock to 97% first
  (§0.2).
- The ISA: `RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats go run ./cmd/probe shaders/X.spv [32|64]`
  and `RADV_DEBUG=asm …` (`MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DISABLE=1` for a repeat).
  Builds are `go generate ./shaders` lines in `shaders/shaders.go`; `.spv`
  is gitignored.
- A GEMM build from disk through H3: `H3_GEMM_SPV=path` (`H3_GEMM_WAVE=32`
  to pin the wave, `H3_GEMM_KRANGE_SPV=path` for the split down
  projection's companion), `H3_GEMM_REF=file` the bit-identical gate
  (written by the first run, compared by every later one); a loaded
  build that is wrong by construction (`L0_LOADS`, `STAGE_L0`) is still
  timed. The clock and power beside it: a 100 ms loop over
  `hwmon/freq1_input` and `power1_average` (G7 will fold it into
  `bench/sysmon.go`).
- The vertical screens: VIDEO.md M7/M11c/M11h (`H3_SHAPES=480 H3_PROFILE=1
  H3_BANK=q8`, `H3_ATTN_SPV`, `H3_CHUNK`), the image DiT's ladder in
  `research/stage-4-dit-graph.md`, Kev's `cmd/kevload`, the LLM's
  `cmd/llm -bench` (memory: it needs `LLM_BANK_CACHE`).
- A MoE GEMM build from disk: `LLM_MOE_SPV=up_q4k_m4=path.spv[,…]`
  (`cmd/llm` needs `-model` as the **shard**, not the checkpoint
  directory, which holds four GGUFs and is refused; before trusting a
  pass, load a wrong-by-construction build through the same override
  and see the gate fail)
  (`LLM_MOE_SPV_WAVE=32` for a wave32 build; `LLM_MOE_PAD=64` for a build
  without `-DSHORT`, since §2.12 the schedule aligns to 16 and a plain
  build would write the next expert's rows; the shared expert runs the
  `q80` builds of the same rungs) on `cmd/llm -moe` and on the
  `llm` tests, which run from `llm/`; `cmd/llm -moe -model <shard>
  -tokens 2048 -iters 60` is ~2 s of device time an arm, so the clock is
  the median of the samples above 100 W.
- The GEMM alone against its row count: `H3_SAWTOOTH=480x864
  ./dit.test -test.run TestGPUGEMMSawtooth` (§2.14; 80 s after staging,
  the same `H3_GEMM_SPV` override); `H3_FUSE=0` on `TestGPUShapes` runs
  the fused epilogues' controls (the v pack, the SwiGLU pass), and a
  fused-path run is gated by `H3_GEMM_REF` against a shipped-build
  reference from the same day.
- Never edit a shader during a sweep; build the test binary to the
  scratchpad first, and check `ps` for another device run.
- Driver pinned in the record: Mesa 26.2.2 (RADV), glslc 2026.3, Vulkan
  1.4.354, kernel 7.1.8. A driver upgrade re-runs G0.

for IQ4_NL alone. **Next:** the m4 rung's 1.90x padding at 2048 (the
largest term left in the up kernel), the Q5_K up build, the down mode's
A fragment loads; and G4 or G6 as KERNELS.md's order says.

**2026-09-29, session 5: G-o8 answered, the GEMM at 85% per clock.**
The remaining points of `lds_w32` were not the LDS's: a probe that adds
the kernel's parts back to the register-only WMMA loop
(`shaders/wmma_issue_probe.comp`, `PEAK_SPV` on `cmd/bench peak`) shows
**every VALU instruction costs the matrix pipe about a clock** on this
part, the GEMM's LDS reads cost 3%, a barrier alone nothing and the two
together 9%. The shipped build's disassembly carried ~40 `v_swap`/`v_mov`
a tile (the allocator assembling the second K tile's fragments under
hoisted staging loads), ~7% of the pipe. Keeping the slab's two tiles as
a loop (`-DKT_LOOP=1 -DSTAGE_RW=1`, now in the `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32`
generate lines) removes them, bit-identical: **projections 40.4 → 43.5
TFLOP/s, 80 → 85% per clock, a 480p forward 27.30 → 26.71 s**; `research/
2.10-…` has the ladder. Measured dead the same session: the 16-lane
exchange that halves LDS bytes (`v_permlanex16` is VALU: −5%), a finer
load order (a wash), a four-wave 128×128 workgroup (−11%). **Left in the
GEMM**: the barrier's lockstep, bounded at ≤ 9 points by the no-barrier
arm, with no LDS room for a deeper slab. **Next:** G4 (attention, whose
head-128 builds spill 112–126 *and* will carry the same kind of moves:
count them first, G-o9), or G5 (int8 in registers, now knowing each VALU
op of a dequant costs a matrix clock: the budget is a few instructions a
MMA, which argues for `v_perm`/`v_cvt_pk` sequences over per-element
work). Gate chain for the new build (every host's own gate) ran this
session; the table in G8 stands for the per-host numbers, this build is
the same kernel one loop deeper.

**2026-09-29, session 4: G8 carried to every host.** All nine hosts run
`dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` pinned to wave32, every gate passing (table
in G8): image step −5.6%, VAE decode −4.3%, Kev's fp16 pass 1.16x at 494
tokens; the build loses below ~1000 rows, so `ace/dit` keeps the wave64
build up to `bigW64Rows` (1024), and the VAE's bias-padded K rounds to
32. Also added: `ACE_DIT_BIG=w64|small` on `TestGPUStepTiming`; the
served binary still needs a redeploy. **Next:** G-o8 (the LDS-side 18
points), or G4 (attention), or G5 (int8 in registers: Kev's fp16 rung
now beats its int8 one at 494 tokens, which says the int8 kernels are
where the LDS round trip still costs).

**2026-09-29, session 3: G2 done and shipped for H3.** The prefetch is
LDS at wave32, not registers: `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` (+ `_krange`)
is bit-identical to the wave64 build and takes H3's projections 37 → 41
TFLOP/s, the split down projection 29 → 41 and a 480p forward 29.9 →
27.1 s (two runs, 0.2%), 74 → 80% per clock; `research/2.9-…` has the
twelve-rung ladder. Three facts for anyone touching the GEMM next: a
wave64 fragment is 8 VGPRs (4x replicated), ACO cannot carry a fragment
across a loop back-edge without copying it element by element (so
register pipelining of coopmat operands is dead on Mesa 26.2.2), and
LDS fragment reads are `ds_load_b64` (pitch 36 halves). Tools: `SR`,
`PIPE`, `DB`, `LDS_STAGE` (`A_LPITCH`/`B_LPITCH`, `BK_TILES` 1–2),
`STAGE_L0`, `LOAD_ORDER` in `dit_gemm.comp`; `H3_GEMM_WAVE`,
`H3_GEMM_KRANGE_SPV`, `H3_GEMM_REF` in `TestGPUShapes`; a `wave` field
on H3's GEMM variant table. **Next:** G8 for the eight other hosts of
the 128×256 kernel (pin wave32, K % 32, each vertical's screen; the
image DiT's `dit.qkv` at M = 4096 is the number the record quotes), then
G-o8 or G4 (attention, whose head-128 builds spill 112–126 and whose
fragments are the same 8 VGPRs). The suite (`gemm_wmma.comp`) was not
ported; the lever was proved on H3's shapes with the bit-identical gate
and the clock instead, which G2's gate asked for in the other order.

**2026-09-29, session 2: G0 and G1 done.** The ceiling is the hardware's
(480 FLOP/clk/CU, flat across chains and wave size). **The clock under a
real kernel is 2600–2650 MHz at ~149 W**, so a video forward's ceiling is
49.9 TFLOP/s and the shipped GEMM is at 74% of it, the attention 75%;
32 busy CPU threads halve the clock (a forward 1.67x slower), which is
M11f's mechanism. The GEMM's loop has no cross-tile prefetch and
recomputes 85 address instructions an iteration; its rate is flat from
1 to 3+ workgroups a CU; with every load an L0 hit it reaches 82–85%
per clock. So: ~10 points memory, ~16 points in-wave schedule. **Next is
G2** in the order above: strength-reduced addresses, then a one-tile
register prefetch, screened with `H3_GEMM_SPV` at 480p and in the suite,
bit-identical via `TestGPUForward`. Tools added: `cmd/probe` (restored),
`-DWAVE`/`-DACC` peak variants, `-DLDS_PAD` and `-DL0_LOADS` screening
knobs in `dit_gemm.comp` (never shipped builds), `H3_GEMM_SPV`. The
scratchpad sampler is not in the tree (G7).

**2026-09-29, session 1: the vertical reopened.** Record assembled from
`research/ideas.md`, `stage-4-dit-graph.md`, `stage-3-dit-attention.md`,
VIDEO.md M11c–M11h and `results/*.csv`. New facts today: the suite's
best GEMM ran at **2813 MHz and 137 W** where the peak probe ran at 2899
and 110, so the per-clock utilisation is 72.6% (39.0) and 76–78% (42.0,
clock unrecorded); the shipped GEMM is **240 VGPRs, no spill, no LDS,
`BK_TILES 1`, no hoist**; both shipped head-128 attentions spill 112–126
VGPRs; `cmd/probe` was deleted on 2026-09-22 by accident and is
**restored** (`cmd/probe/main.go`, from `501053a^`). Outside numbers:
36.9 TFLOP/s is the best public figure on this chip, 92% of peak is what
rocBLAS reaches on a 7900 XTX. Nothing else built. Next: G0, then G1.

package qwen

// InterleaveGLU lays a SwiGLU's gate and up projections ([n, k] each) out
// as one [2n, k] weight in groups of 64 rows -- 32 gate rows, then the up
// rows of the same 32 outputs -- which is what dit_gemm.comp's C_SWIGLU
// epilogue is built on (KERNELS.md G3, research §2.14): a 64-column block
// of the fused GEMM then holds 32 gate columns and the up columns of the
// same 32 outputs, so a wave's four accumulator tiles are gate 0-1 and up
// 0-1 of one layout. dst holds 2*n*k.
func InterleaveGLU(dst, gate, up []float32, n, k int) {
	if n%32 != 0 {
		panic("qwen: InterleaveGLU wants n a multiple of 32")
	}
	parallelFor(n/32, func(g int) {
		copy(dst[(64*g)*k:(64*g+32)*k], gate[32*g*k:(32*g+32)*k])
		copy(dst[(64*g+32)*k:(64*g+64)*k], up[32*g*k:(32*g+32)*k])
	})
}

package qwen

// InterleaveGLU lays a SwiGLU's gate and up projections ([n, k] each) out
// as one [2n, k] weight in groups of 64 rows -- 32 gate rows, then the up
// rows of the same 32 outputs -- which is what dit_gemm.comp's C_SWIGLU
// epilogue is built on (KERNELS.md G3, research §2.14): a 64-column block
// of the fused GEMM then holds 32 gate columns and the up columns of the
// same 32 outputs, so a wave's four accumulator tiles are gate 0-1 and up
// 0-1 of one layout. dst holds 2*n*k.
func InterleaveGLU(dst, gate, up []float32, n, k int) {
	if n%32 != 0 {
		panic("qwen: InterleaveGLU wants n a multiple of 32")
	}
	parallelFor(n/32, func(g int) {
		copy(dst[(64*g)*k:(64*g+32)*k], gate[32*g*k:(32*g+32)*k])
		copy(dst[(64*g+32)*k:(64*g+64)*k], up[32*g*k:(32*g+32)*k])
	})
}

#version 450
#extension GL_EXT_shader_16bit_storage : require
#extension GL_EXT_shader_explicit_arithmetic_types_float16 : require
// Zero pc.tokens rows of pc.dim halves, pc.lda apart, at pc.outOff in the
// fp16 arena: a GEMM's A operand pad rows ahead of a GEMM whose epilogue
// writes its pad rows where a consumer reads them (KERNELS.md G3: the v
// projection stored as the attention's fragment tiles, whose pad keys must
// be +0 like the pack's -- a -0 behind a zero mask moves a WMMA sum an ulp).
// One workgroup a row, 256 lanes along it.

#include "dit_common.glsl"

layout(binding = 2) buffer HAct { float16_t hact[]; };

layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

void main() {
    uint r = gl_WorkGroupID.x;
    if (r >= pc.tokens) {
        return;
    }
    uint dst = pc.outOff + r * pc.lda;
    for (uint c = gl_LocalInvocationID.x; c < pc.dim; c += 256u) {
        hact[dst + c] = float16_t(0.0);
    }
}

Stage letter **A** (ACE), since M is video. Code in `ace/`: `plan`, `dit` (+ `Detokenize`), `vae`, `lm` (A7: the 5 Hz LM), `pipeline` (A6 DiT-only, A8 `Options.Think` after `LoadLM`); `cmd/ace` thinks by default (`-think=false` = A6). The user listened 2026-09-27: sounds great. A9: the user chose a submit-then-poll endpoint → `/v1/music` in `/v1/videos`' shape (`api/music.go`, `backend/music.go`, `serve -music`), reading ACE-Step's release_task field names/aliases; unsupported upstream fields are 400s. `-music` is not in the deployed ai.service unit (user's call). A12 (2026-09-27): sample mode (`sample_query`, `cmd/ace -sample`) — needs `models/ACE-Step-1.5-src/acestep/genres_vocab.txt`; FSM understand phase, genres trie (no leading space: `genres:synthwave`), three deliberate departures from upstream's API recorded in MUSIC.md A12. A10 (2026-09-27): int8 LM layers (`lm.BankQ8`, the default; `-lm-fp16` / `-music-lm-fp16` the control), head stays fp16; step 22 ms at the bus; host top-p bucketed (10 → 1 ms). A11 (2026-09-27): audio in — `ace/vae.Encoder`, `dit.GPU.Tokenize`, `ace/pipeline/tasks.go` (`Options.Audio`), `/v1/music` multipart `src_audio`/`reference_audio` (server `*_path` fields refused on purpose), `cmd/ace -task/-src/-ref`; oracle `reference/dump_ace_tasks.py [--bf16]`. Nothing planned after the freeze.

- **The VAE encoder is precision-hungry at 48 kHz**: fp16 audio alone costs the posterior 45 dB, block 0's inputs 51. Fixed by carrying them as fp16 hi+lo pairs against duplicated weights (56–63 dB; bf16 is 16–19). **`float16_t(v)` then `v - float(hi)` is folded to lo = 0 by the compiler** — cut the mantissa with a bit mask instead; a teacher-forced single conv showed it.
- **A cover's fidelity rides on code flips**: a code at an FSQ floor boundary flips and replaces 5 hint rows. Upstream's own unseeded posterior noise flips 2 of 150; bf16 flips 73. Price covers against bf16, and gate the tokenizer as "differs only within a margin of the boundary".

- **ace/lm's device graph** reuses one fp16 fragment-tiled weight for both DiT GEMM rungs (prefill) and `llm_gemv.comp` (1-3 rows, decode); new `ace_lm_prep`/`ace_lm_attn` shaders over a KV cache (row = token, slot, position). 45 ms a step for 1 or 2 rows (CFG row free), bandwidth-bound.
- **Qwen3-4B's SwiGLU product hits 6.39e4 (layer 16, a newline)** — ffScale 1/16, undone by the add's gate. A missing barrier in ace_lm_prep NaN'd ~1 layer in 12 and hid behind it; `TestDeterministic` guards that class.
- Upstream quirks A7/A8 had to reproduce: phase-2 CoT is PyYAML-dumped (width-80 folding; `no` → `'no'`), top-p on untempered logits, FSM caption ends on the raw argmax after a newline, language top-1 forced, codes switch the DiT task to `cover` (instruction "Generate audio semantic tokens…"), the CoT's language never reaches the DiT (read as `vocal_language`), T = 5 × codes.
- Torch's fp32 top-p puts the boundary one token off ours sometimes (its softmax denominator 8.7e-6 low); the test tolerates exactly that.
- **Oracle env is `.venv-acestep`** (transformers 4.57.1); upstream's handler overwrites the checkpoint dir's model .py, so the oracle uses `models/ace-checkpoints/checkpoints`. `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. Upstream LM sampling is unseeded: `dump_ace_lm.py` is a trace, not reproducible.
- The HF clones' `.git` dirs were removed 2026-09-27: a clobbered checkpoint file can no longer be restored with git.
- `dump_ace_lm.py` now merges into its manifest; run labels individually (a sample case is ~8 min on the CPU). TestLogits rel bound is 3e-3 (the bpm-value step sits at 2–2.5e-3; KL is the real bound).
- **Price the LM against bf16 over what the FSM leaves open** (`reference/dump_ace_lm_tf.py` → `acelmtf`, `TestBankAgainstBF16`): a forced step's logits choose nothing, and bf16's worst full-vocab steps are exactly those. int8 ≈ bf16 in the CoT, 50× under it in the codes. An int8 head wrecks phase 2 (code logits are head-sensitive, CFG doubles it). Phase 1 must read the whole vocab: upstream leaves the field name after a caption unmasked and codes can hold 1% mass.
- `TestLogits` always stages the fp16 bank (implementation gate); `ACE_LM_BANK=fp16` switches the shared staging.
- A-o1: DiT residual 5.7e5 → fp32; DiT fp16 drift is all layer 0's q/k, priced against upstream bf16 (`underBF16`).

Related: [[video-vertical-minimax-h3]] (same DiT-on-GPU machinery; M11a: price quant vs bf16), [[reference-dumps-python-env]], [[api-follows-openai-standard]] (A-o3: OpenAI has no music endpoint — ask before choosing), [[decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth]].

// Zero pc.tokens rows of pc.dim halves, pc.lda apart, at pc.outOff in the

#include "dit_common.glsl"

layout(binding = 2) buffer HAct { float16_t hact[]; };

layout(local_size_x = 256) in;

void main() {
    uint r = gl_WorkGroupID.x;
    if (r >= pc.tokens) {

Opened and **closed 2026-09-27** at the user's request: `MUSIC.md` was frozen to `research/music-vertical.md` (a code comment citing `MUSIC.md` resolves there); `TODO.md` has a "Music generation — closed" section with the open items (listen to out/ace-a10-*, out/ace-a11-*; not in ai.service; DiT/VAE speed). Stage letter **A** (ACE), since M is video. Code in `ace/`: `plan`, `dit` (+ `Detokenize`), `vae`, `lm` (A7: the 5 Hz LM), `pipeline` (A6 DiT-only, A8 `Options.Think` after `LoadLM`); `cmd/ace` thinks by default (`-think=false` = A6). The user listened 2026-09-27: sounds great. A9: the user chose a submit-then-poll endpoint → `/v1/music` in `/v1/videos`' shape (`api/music.go`, `backend/music.go`, `serve -music`), reading ACE-Step's release_task field names/aliases; unsupported upstream fields are 400s. `-music` is not in the deployed ai.service unit (user's call). A12 (2026-09-27): sample mode (`sample_query`, `cmd/ace -sample`) — needs `models/ACE-Step-1.5-src/acestep/genres_vocab.txt`; FSM understand phase, genres trie (no leading space: `genres:synthwave`), three deliberate departures from upstream's API recorded in MUSIC.md A12. A10 (2026-09-27): int8 LM layers (`lm.BankQ8`, the default; `-lm-fp16` / `-music-lm-fp16` the control), head stays fp16; step 22 ms at the bus; host top-p bucketed (10 → 1 ms). A11 (2026-09-27): audio in — `ace/vae.Encoder`, `dit.GPU.Tokenize`, `ace/pipeline/tasks.go` (`Options.Audio`), `/v1/music` multipart `src_audio`/`reference_audio` (server `*_path` fields refused on purpose), `cmd/ace -task/-src/-ref`; oracle `reference/dump_ace_tasks.py [--bf16]`. Nothing planned after the freeze.

- **The VAE encoder is precision-hungry at 48 kHz**: fp16 audio alone costs the posterior 45 dB, block 0's inputs 51. Fixed by carrying them as fp16 hi+lo pairs against duplicated weights (56–63 dB; bf16 is 16–19). **`float16_t(v)` then `v - float(hi)` is folded to lo = 0 by the compiler** — cut the mantissa with a bit mask instead; a teacher-forced single conv showed it.
- **A cover's fidelity rides on code flips**: a code at an FSQ floor boundary flips and replaces 5 hint rows. Upstream's own unseeded posterior noise flips 2 of 150; bf16 flips 73. Price covers against bf16, and gate the tokenizer as "differs only within a margin of the boundary".

- **ace/lm's device graph** reuses one fp16 fragment-tiled weight for both DiT GEMM rungs (prefill) and `llm_gemv.comp` (1-3 rows, decode); new `ace_lm_prep`/`ace_lm_attn` shaders over a KV cache (row = token, slot, position). 45 ms a step for 1 or 2 rows (CFG row free), bandwidth-bound.
- **Qwen3-4B's SwiGLU product hits 6.39e4 (layer 16, a newline)** — ffScale 1/16, undone by the add's gate. A missing barrier in ace_lm_prep NaN'd ~1 layer in 12 and hid behind it; `TestDeterministic` guards that class.
- Upstream quirks A7/A8 had to reproduce: phase-2 CoT is PyYAML-dumped (width-80 folding; `no` → `'no'`), top-p on untempered logits, FSM caption ends on the raw argmax after a newline, language top-1 forced, codes switch the DiT task to `cover` (instruction "Generate audio semantic tokens…"), the CoT's language never reaches the DiT (read as `vocal_language`), T = 5 × codes.
- Torch's fp32 top-p puts the boundary one token off ours sometimes (its softmax denominator 8.7e-6 low); the test tolerates exactly that.
- **Oracle env is `.venv-acestep`** (transformers 4.57.1); upstream's handler overwrites the checkpoint dir's model .py, so the oracle uses `models/ace-checkpoints/checkpoints`. `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. Upstream LM sampling is unseeded: `dump_ace_lm.py` is a trace, not reproducible.
- The HF clones' `.git` dirs were removed 2026-09-27: a clobbered checkpoint file can no longer be restored with git.
- `dump_ace_lm.py` now merges into its manifest; run labels individually (a sample case is ~8 min on the CPU). TestLogits rel bound is 3e-3 (the bpm-value step sits at 2–2.5e-3; KL is the real bound).
- **Price the LM against bf16 over what the FSM leaves open** (`reference/dump_ace_lm_tf.py` → `acelmtf`, `TestBankAgainstBF16`): a forced step's logits choose nothing, and bf16's worst full-vocab steps are exactly those. int8 ≈ bf16 in the CoT, 50× under it in the codes. An int8 head wrecks phase 2 (code logits are head-sensitive, CFG doubles it). Phase 1 must read the whole vocab: upstream leaves the field name after a caption unmasked and codes can hold 1% mass.
- `TestLogits` always stages the fp16 bank (implementation gate); `ACE_LM_BANK=fp16` switches the shared staging.
- A-o1: DiT residual 5.7e5 → fp32; DiT fp16 drift is all layer 0's q/k, priced against upstream bf16 (`underBF16`).

Related: [[video-vertical-minimax-h3]] (same DiT-on-GPU machinery; M11a: price quant vs bf16), [[reference-dumps-python-env]], [[api-follows-openai-standard]] (A-o3: OpenAI has no music endpoint — ask before choosing), [[decode-is-latency-not-bandwidth]].

20	// The shape of the work is what decides the graph. One decoder call is a
21	// tile-clip: 7 latent frames × 16 × 16 latents = 1,792 tokens, plus 4
22	// registers and a zero token, 1,797 rows of full attention. A 480p 5 s
23	// decode is 105 of them and a 768p one 196, all the same length and all
24	// independent. So they run **batched**: S sequences side by side at a row
25	// stride of 1,808 (a whole number of 16-row tiles), every row-local stage —
26	// the norms, all seven projections, SwiGLU, the gates — one dispatch over
27	// all S·1,808 rows, and only the attention per sequence (its planes offset
28	// to the sequence's first tile). The GEMMs then see M ≈ 14k at S = 8, where
29	// the image DiT's kernels are at their measured rate, instead of 1.8k.
30	//
31	// What differs from the transformer, and why:
32	//
33	//   - **Biases ride in the GEMM.** Every projection here has one and the
34	//     transformer's have none. Each A operand carries a column of ones just
35	//     past its real width and each weight its bias in that column (K padded
36	//     to the next tile), so a projection and its bias are one GEMM, in fp16
37	//     as the pipeline's own fp16 autocast has them. proj_in does the same
38	//     with one-hot columns for the four register tokens, so the whole
39	//     sequence's input — patches, registers, the zero token — is one GEMM
40	//     straight into the residual.
41	//   - **fp16 throughout, residual aside.** M5's oracle has every activation
42	//     of the stack under 832 (the FFN's down projection output; its input
43	//     peaks at 354), so no operand needs the transformer's 1/16 FFN scale.
44	//     The residual is fp32 because it is cheap to, not because it must be.
45	//   - **Stale keys are harmless here**, which they were not in M7. The
46	//     attention reads whole 64-key blocks and masks the keys past its count
47	//     out of P but not out of the row max, so a sequence's last block reads
48	//     the next sequence's first keys into its max. q and k are RMS-normed
49	//     per head with no weight, so every score is at most |q||k|/8 = 8 and a
50	//     foreign key can only move the max by a bounded amount, never
51	//     underflow a real weight. The planes are zeroed at allocation, and
52	//     every row the attention can read is written by a pack before it is.
53	type GPU struct {
54		// Between, when set, is called between two submissions, when nothing
55		// of this model's is on the device. A server uses it to let other work
56		// run inside a forward that holds the device for tens of seconds, and
57		// an error from it (a cancelled request) abandons the run there
58		// (VIDEO.md M9).
59		Between func() error
60	
61		dev *vk.Device
62		cfg *Config
63	
64		wbuf, abuf, hbuf *vk.Buffer
65		banks            []*vk.Buffer
66		pipes            map[string]*vk.ComputePipeline
67		gemms            []map[gemmKernel]*vk.ComputePipeline
68		attnPipes        map[AttnVariant]*vk.ComputePipeline
69		// attn is the build blockPass records; attnProbed says the first run
70		// has chosen it (the probe is a dispatch, so a staging can't), and
71		// attnFixed that a test has.
72		attn                  AttnVariant
73		attnProbed, attnFixed bool
74		mods                  []*vk.ShaderModule
75	
76		H, ffn, heads, headDim, ropeHalf int
77		seqLen, stride, maxSeqs, maxRows int // tokens a sequence, its row stride, sequences a batch
78		tileH, tileW                     int // latents a tile, for which the rope table is built
79		kH, kF, kIn                      int // K of the projections off H, off the FFN, and proj_in
80		ldaH, ldaF, ldaIn                int
81	
82		blocks  []blockW
83		projIn  headW
84		projOut headW
85		outBias []float32 // proj_out.bias + proj_out.weight · norm_out.bias, fp32
86	
87		// wbuf (fp32): the rope tables for maxRows rows, the q/k norm's ones.
88		wCos, wSin, wOnes uint32
89		// abuf (fp32, host-cached: the host reads the output back): the
90		// residual, the scratch, the per-block vectors, the output.
91		aX, aS, aOut     uint32
92		aZeros, aNormOut uint32
93		actElems         int
94		// hbuf (fp16): the q/k/v planes and the A operands.
95		hQ, hK, hV, hA, hCtx, hFFN, hIn uint32
96		planeRows, hElems               int
97	}
98	
99	type headW struct {
100		bank int
101		off  uint32
102		n, k int
103	}
104	
105	// blockW is where a block's weights live: the fp16 projections in a bank,
106	// and its fp32 vectors in the activation arena, which is where the norm and
107	// gate kernels read them.
108	type blockW struct {
109		bank                 int
110		off                  map[proj]uint32
111		norm1, norm2, s1, s2 uint32
112	}
113	
114	type proj int
115	
116	const (
117		projQ proj = iota
118		projK
119		projV
120		projO
121		projGate // the silu'd half of ff.net.0.proj, rows [ffn, 2·ffn)
122		projUp   // the linear half, rows [0, ffn)
123		projDown
124	)
125	
126	var projOrder = []proj{projQ, projK, projV, projO, projGate, projUp, projDown}
127	
128	// pushConstants mirrors shaders/dit_common.glsl.
129	type pushConstants struct {
130		InOff, OutOff, WOff uint32
131		Tokens, Dim, Heads  uint32
132		HeadDim, Span       uint32
133		KOff, VOff, KStride uint32
134		Eps, Scale          uint32
135		Aux0, Aux1, Aux2    uint32
136		BOff                uint32
137		GemmM, GemmN, GemmK uint32
138		LDA, LDB            uint32
139	}
140	
141	func (p pushConstants) bytes() []byte {
142		out := make([]byte, unsafe.Sizeof(p))
143		*(*pushConstants)(unsafe.Pointer(&out[0])) = p
144		return out
145	}
146	
147	type gemmKernel int
148	
149	const gemmBig gemmKernel = 0 // 128x256 tiles, the image DiT's measured winner
150	
151	var gemmVariants = map[gemmKernel]struct {
152		spirv  []byte
153		bm, bn int
154		bk     int    // the K tile: 32 for the LDS-staged build, 16 otherwise
155		wave   uint32 // a pinned subgroup size, or 0 for the device's default
156	}{
157		// The LDS-staged wave32 build (KERNELS.md G2, research §2.9), bit-identical
158		// to the wave64 one it replaced.
159		gemmBig: {shaders.DiTGEMMWG128x256LDSW32, 128, 256, 32, 32},
160	}
161	
162	const (
163		tile     = 16
164		gemmPad  = 128
165		rowAlign = 128 // the big GEMM's M tile
166		log2e    = 1.4426950408889634
167		// maxBankBytes is one storage buffer's range on this device.
168		maxBankBytes = 0xfffffffc
169		// maxKeyBlock is the longest key block the attention reads past its count.
170		maxKeyBlock = 8 * tile
171	)
172	
173	func roundUp(n, m int) int { return (n + m - 1) / m * m }
174	
175	// NewGPU stages the decoder (4.9 GB of fp16) for tiles of tileH × tileW
176	// latents, maxSeqs tile-clips a batch.
177	func NewGPU(dev *vk.Device, dir string, tileH, tileW, maxSeqs int) (*GPU, error) {
178		cfg, err := LoadConfig(dir)
179		if err != nil {
180			return nil, err
181		}
182		if maxSeqs < 1 {
183			return nil, fmt.Errorf("vae: %d sequences a batch", maxSeqs)
184		}
185		g := &GPU{
186			dev: dev, cfg: cfg, pipes: map[string]*vk.ComputePipeline{},
187			H: cfg.Hidden(), ffn: cfg.FFN(), heads: cfg.Heads, headDim: cfg.HeadDim, ropeHalf: cfg.RopeWidth() / 2,
188			tileH: tileH, tileW: tileW, maxSeqs: maxSeqs,
189		}
190		g.seqLen = cfg.ClipTokens()*tileH*tileW + cfg.Registers + 1
191		g.stride = roundUp(g.seqLen, tile)
192		g.maxRows = roundUp(maxSeqs*g.stride, rowAlign)
193		// One column past the real width for the bias, K padded to the big
194		// GEMM's K tile (32 since KERNELS.md G2; the pad columns are zero in
195		// every A operand and every weight).
196		bk := gemmVariants[gemmBig].bk
197		g.kH, g.kF = roundUp(g.H+1, bk), roundUp(g.ffn+1, bk)
198		g.kIn = roundUp(cfg.LatentChannels+1+cfg.Registers, bk)
199		g.ldaH, g.ldaF, g.ldaIn = g.kH+gemmPad, g.kF+gemmPad, g.kIn+gemmPad
200	
201		set, err := safetensors.OpenSet(dir)
202		if err != nil {
203			return nil, err
204		}
205		defer set.Close()
206		for _, step := range []func(*safetensors.Set) error{g.alloc, g.stage, g.build} {
207			if err := step(set); err != nil {
208				g.Destroy()
209				return nil, err
210			}
211		}
212		return g, nil
213	}
214	
215	// packB narrows a [n, k] row-major weight into 16x16 fragment tiles,
216	// kt-fastest: dit_gemm.comp's B layout.
217	func packB(dst []uint16, w []float32, n, k int) {
218		kt := k / tile
219		parallelFor((n+63)/64, func(c int) {
220			for i := c * 64; i < min((c+1)*64, n); i++ {
221				row := w[i*k : (i+1)*k]
222				base := (i / tile) * kt * tile * tile
223				lane := (i % tile) * tile
224				for j, v := range row {
225					dst[base+(j/tile)*tile*tile+lane+j%tile] = safetensors.F32ToF16(v)
226				}
227			}
228		})
229	}

content.content:
interleaved by `qwen.InterleaveGLU` at staging, the int8 and fp16 banks
alike; `gemmLDSW32GLU` when the big kernel is the LDS build, the fused
GEMM with the fp32 store and the interleaved SwiGLU pass on every other
arm and as the control, `SetFuseGLU` / `QIMAGE_FUSE=0`).
`TestGPUFusedEpilogues` holds a prefill and a cached step at 256²
bit-identical to the control on both banks, `TestGPUOracle256` passes
unchanged, and at 1024² on the served int8 bank:

| | cached step, per dispatch (`TestGPUStepProfile`, two runs) | cached step, wall (`TestGPUGEMMScreen`, LDS arm, two runs) | prefill, per dispatch |
|---|---|---|---|
| control (the fused GEMM + the SwiGLU pass) | 1.990 / 1.984 s (`swiglu` 82–83 ms, 4.2%) | 2044 / 2046 ms | 2.065 / 2.059 s |
| **the SwiGLU epilogue** | **1.905 / 1.911 s** | **1929 / 1968 ms** | **1.979 / 1.984 s** |

**1.04–1.06x a step**, the fused GEMM itself 615–617 → 602–605 ms (the
fp16 store is the cheaper one here) and the other four arms of the
screen within 0.3% between the two runs, which is the control on the
control. The v store is **not carried** there: the image DiT's fresh
k/v rows land under a cached prefix at their global rows, and a t2i
prefix is 19 text rows, so the fresh rows start mid-tile where `C_PACK`
addresses whole tiles; padding the prefix to a tile touches the layout,
the masks and the KV cache for ~24 ms of a 1.9 s step (`pack v`, 1.2%).

**Left.** The q/k packs (`qkpack`, 1.1% each: a per-head RMS norm over
128 components, which spans two waves of the GEMM's 64-column tile, then
RoPE) stay passes. `C_F16` for anything else has no consumer here: o and
down feed the fp32 residual. The carry-in (G8) continues with `ace/dit`, the VAE and the speech
encoders, each with the same two passes; the LDS build's `C_PACK`/`C_SWIGLU`
are host changes there now (the interleaved weight and a `gemmWith`), with
each vertical's own gate.

**Tools.** `-DSTORE_TILES=n` (pricing), `-DC_SWIGLU=1` and the lifted
`C_PACK`/`C_F16` guard on `dit_gemm.comp`'s LDS build; `zero_f16.comp`;
`-DINTERLEAVE=32` on `dit_swiglu_f16.comp`; `TestGPUGEMMSawtooth`
(`H3_SAWTOOTH=<h>x<w>`, `H3_SAWTOOTH_REPS`), `H3_FUSE=0` on

---
name: kernels-vertical-reopened
description: "The kernel-optimisation vertical was reopened 2026-09-29 as root KERNELS.md (G-stages); the ceiling is per clock, and cmd/probe is the ISA tool"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 18123f91-ab01-40e1-b663-e0bf82d8c3e6
  modified: 2026-09-30T00:40:00.000Z
---

Root `KERNELS.md` (opened 2026-09-29, G-stages) is the live plan for taking the WMMA kernels from 42.0 toward 55.5 TFLOP/s. Facts a session needs before touching it: the suite's best GEMM ran at 2813 MHz / 137 W where the `peak` probe ran 2899 / 110, so utilisation is quoted per clock (478 FLOP/clk/CU is the measured peak); the shipped `dit_gemm_wg128x256_bt16_swz8` is 240 VGPRs, no spill, `BK_TILES 1`, no prefetch; both head-128 attentions spill 112–126 VGPRs. `cmd/probe` (RADV_DEBUG=shaderstats/asm) was deleted by accident on 2026-09-22 and restored 2026-09-29.

G0/G1 (2026-09-29, research §0.6, §6.5): **no real kernel runs at 2899 MHz.** A video forward runs at 2600–2650 MHz and ~149 W (package-limited ~150 W), so its ceiling is 49.9 TFLOP/s, not 55.5; a 20 ms bench burst sees 2813. **32 busy CPU threads halve the GPU clock** and make a forward 1.67x slower: never run a CPU-heavy job (staging, audio decode, a test sweep) beside a device timing, and sample `hwmon/freq1_input` + `power1_average` around any in-pipeline number. The shipped GEMM's rate is flat from 1 to 3+ workgroups a CU, and ACO does not prefetch across K tiles.

G2 (2026-09-29, research §2.9): the GEMM ships as `dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32` (+ `_krange`) for H3: K slabs staged through LDS at wave32, 4x4 tiles, eight waves, bit-identical, 74 → 80% per clock, a 480p forward 29.9 → 27.1 s. G8 (same day) carried it to all nine hosts through their own gates: image step 2179 → 2058 ms, VAE decode 37.1 → 35.5 s, Kev fp16 at 494 tokens 154 → 132 ms; it loses below ~1000 rows ([[lds-gemm-needs-a-full-machine]]). The mechanism and what it rules out: [[coopmat-fragments-cost-8-vgprs]]; the screen: [[h3-gemm-screen-recipe]].

G5 (2026-09-29, research §2.11): started as "Q4 B fragments built in registers" and measured out of it before it was built. On the LLM's MoE up GEMM (`llm_moe_gemm.comp`) the LDS round trip is ~8 points and the loop without its stagings already runs at the pipe; the cost was the dependent, divergent bank-load chain in front of every K-step, each block's lines re-read 2–8x. The K loop as a software pipeline with each block's bytes fetched once (`-DPIPE=2`) is bit-identical, `moe.up` 1.68x at 2048 tokens, whole-model prefill 1194 → 1407 tok/s. The same pipeline on the down mode moves Q5_1 by nothing and IQ4_NL by 1.05x (shipped for IQ4_NL only). Lesson: price a kernel's parts by their absence (`MOE_*` knobs, `LLM_MOE_SPV`, [[moe-gemm-screening]]) before building the arm the plan names; a two-set (ping-pong) register pipeline spilled and lost, the one-set form won.

G5c (2026-09-30, research §2.12): the padding. The permutation aligns experts to one fragment (16 rows) instead of the widest row block, and every single-wave build of `llm_moe_gemm.comp` is a `SHORT` build that runs one of WM copies of its K loop from the record's real-row count, bit-identical: the padding factor at 2048 tokens 1.90x → 1.19x, `moe.down` 1.23x (1.28x on IQ4_NL), `moe.up` 1.11x, prefill 1417 → 1514 tok/s at 2048; the m2/m4 boundary moved to 256 tokens. Two facts: any third copy of the Q4_K up m4 loop spills 15 registers and costs 9% on full blocks (it ships 2- and 4-tile copies, the store bounded by the real count), and a short tile's rows are cheap rows (0.086 vs 0.137 µs) because the slab unpack, ~300 VALU a lane a step, is now the largest term in the up projection. Next on that kernel: the unpack's VALU.

**Why:** eight verticals ended on "the GEMMs are at their ceiling" without the ceiling ever being pushed; a GEMM win lands in every served request.

**How to apply:** file a closed finding under the next free `§N.M` in `research/` and point the G-stage at it; prove a lever in `gemm_wmma.comp`'s suite first, ship it in `dit_gemm.comp`, and screen it with each vertical's own tool ([[strix-halo-bench-runs]], [[never-edit-source-during-a-sweep]]).

**2026-09-30 (G4, §3.8):** the transposed attention priced and left as shipped — the honest floor is 81% per clock (87–90% with L0 hits), the softmax 6–7 points, the K/V loads 11–12, and five bit-identical arms all inside ±2% of the shipped build; G4b (K/V slabs through LDS at QT1) is the one lever left, ≤ 2% of a forward. The kernel is opt-in on the image DiT (`QIMAGE_ATTN_T=1`, 1.7% a step) because the edit oracle's prefill bound sits near its sensitivity floor. See [[attention-kernel-plateau]]. Next in the order: G6 (streaming kernels) or G3 (the epilogue).

**G3 done 2026-09-30** (§2.14): the fp32 C store costs the matrix pipe nothing (`STORE_TILES` control, same per-clock rate); the M sawtooth is ≤ 5% past ~1300 rows; H3's `pack v` and `swiglu` passes are the LDS build's epilogue now (`C_PACK`, `C_SWIGLU` with `projGateUp` interleaved in 64-row groups; `zero_f16.comp` for the A pad rows), bit-identical, a 480p forward 26.2 → 25.6 s. The served binary restages its int8 cache once on redeploy. The SwiGLU fusion is carried to `qimage/dit` too (same session, 1.04–1.06x a cached step; the v store is not, a 19-row prefix puts fresh rows mid-tile). Next: `ace/dit`, the VAE, the speech encoders (G8); then G6.

content.text:
G8's remaining carry-in is done: the two G3 fusions (v stored straight from its GEMM, gate|up as one GEMM ending in the SwiGLU) now run in the music DiT and the video VAE. Both are bit-identical to the binaries before the change, by output hash, and to their in-tree controls. The speech encoders were priced and left.

**Music DiT (`ace/dit`)** — a forward, before → after:

| song length | before | after | gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 30 s (375 rows) | 119.6 ms | 111.4 ms | 1.07x |
| 2 min | 381.8 ms | 347.5 ms | 1.10x |
| 4 min | 803.5 ms | 744.5 ms | 1.08x |
| 10 min | 2260 ms | 2124 ms | 1.06x |

- The fused gate|up runs on the LDS build at every row count, not only above 1024 rows. At 375 rows it is 110 ms against 120 for the wave64 build plus the SwiGLU pass, and it ties at 125 rows. The other projections keep the 1024-row rule.
- All `ace/dit` tests pass, as do `ace/pipeline`'s `TestGenerate` and `TestTasks`.

**Video VAE (`h3/vae`)** — device time for 124 frames:

| | before | after | gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 480p decode | 34.4 s | 30.0 s | 1.15x |
| 768p decode | 64.3 s | 56.0 s | 1.15x |

- PSNR is unchanged at 81.7 dB.
- A second 768p run read 57.4 s at a lower clock (2696 MHz / 129 W), with nothing in the graph to explain it.
- v is stored by its GEMM only when the batch is whole 128-row tiles, which the served batch of 8 is. The VAE's biases ride in the GEMM, so a pad row would be the bias rather than +0; the last partial batch of a decode still runs the pack.

**Speech encoders** — not carried. Parakeet's feed forward is not gated, and it runs a different GEMM rung. Its two SiLU passes and v pack are 2.3% of a 13.5 ms encoder, so a new epilogue build would save at most 0.3 ms a clip. Kokoro was left on the same argument without being measured.

The served binary still needs a redeploy to pick up any of G3; I did not deploy. Nothing is committed by me; the changes are in the working tree for the auto-committer.

I added `TestGPUBits` to `ace/dit` (`ACE_DIT_REF=file` for the cross-binary hash), `bits` hash lines to the VAE decode tests, and `ACE_DIT_FUSE=0` / `H3_VAE_FUSE=0` for the controls. `KERNELS.md` (a new G8 section and the session 11 handoff), `research/2.14-gemm-epilogue.md`, `VIDEO.md` and `TODO.md` carry the numbers.

Next in `KERNELS.md` is G6 (the streaming kernels) or G4b. The VAE has no per-kind profile test, so G6 there should start by writing one.

content.content:
true 885**, 1.28x too fast, with a degenerate indexer selecting a contiguous
  window. **The failure mode is a benchmark that gets faster**, which is the one
  direction nobody audits; the rule it leaves is to price a suspicious win in
  FLOP/s or bytes/s against the device's peak before believing it.
- **`hc.cn` is still at 134 GB/s** where a copy gets 236, and there are now
  **three** spent explanations, not two. P12-4 spent the 256-way tree (deleting
  it outright is 5331.5 µs against 5325.8) and the `gamma` read (5332.9). P15
  spent the **memory type**, which was the most plausible of the three and had
  never been tested: the arenas are HOST_CACHED and this kernel is pure arena
attempted here. **This is the floor of the current format choice, not a
kernel defect**: at 21.1 TFLOP/s and 61 GB/s of bank, `moe.up` is neither
arithmetic-bound on its matrix cores nor bandwidth-bound — it is bound by
unpacking a 4.5-bit bank into fp16 three instructions at a time.

## P12-4: `hc.cn` — both of P11's leads cost nothing

P11 left `hc.cn` at 134 GB/s where a copy gets 236, with two named suspects.
**Both are wrong, and the probes are one line each.**

- **The reduction tree is free.** P11 proposed the norm's tail — "an
  eight-barrier 256-way tree where a subgroup reduction is one barrier" — and
  noted it would not be bit-exact. Deleting the tree outright (wrong answer,
  right cost) measures **5331.5 µs against 5325.8** at 8192 tokens. The eight
  barriers and the 256-way tree, four times a token, cost **nothing at all**.
  So the non-bit-exact rewrite that was queued behind it would have bought
  zero, and `llm_hc_norm.comp` does not have to move.
- **The gamma read is free.** The other candidate was the kernel's load count:
  each of the four streams reads a 10 KB `gamma` row per token, a third of all
  its memory operations. Replacing it with a constant measures **5332.9 µs**.
  It is the same 40 KB for every token and the MALL serves it.

So `hc.cn`'s 57% of copy bandwidth is neither its barriers nor its redundant
loads, and it is still unexplained. What is now ruled out is everything that
was on the list.

## P12-5: the block skip hoisted out of the loop is worth zero at prefill

The one structural idea tried and reverted. At 64 000 cells a query tile walks
~2000 key blocks and P11-7 measured only 25.9% of them live, so ~1480 blocks
pay a **dependent** global read — the loop cannot decide to skip until the
block's mask words come back — and then do nothing with it. That is P8/P9/P10's
shape one level up, and it predicted well: a cost model in which a dead block
  be recoverable — which would make 4096 free and 8192 worth having. The probe
  is to stage the wide arenas and prefill in narrow chunks anyway, which
  separates *allocated* from *used*.
- **The ubatch ladder itself has not flattened**: 2048 → 8192 is 1.16x on the
  graph (1207.7 → 1403.9). Whether any of that survives the decode trade above
  is unmeasured.
- **`hc.cn` at 134 GB/s** is now the cleanest unexplained number in the
  prefill graph *and* has no remaining hypothesis — P12-4 spent both. The
  next probe should be the access pattern itself: it runs four read-modify-write
  streams plus an fp16 write per token, where a copy runs two.
- **`attn.select` at 64 000 cells** is untouched and is 7.5% of a prefill
  token there. It streams the row out of DRAM five times — four radix passes
  and an emit, 1.28 MB a token a layer — at ~133 GB/s. The two routes are
it. The activation arenas come from a HOST_CACHED memory type, because the host
reads them at 24.76 GB/s there against 0.18 on the write-combined type the
device-local heap offers. The file says outright that this is "a claim about
GPU time, and a claim like that needs a run with the knob the other way".

The claim was worth re-testing because **the allocation it was made about grew
by two orders**: since P13/P14 the KV planes share that buffer, which is
3.85 GB at 139 000 cells, and `hc.cn` — a kernel that is pure arena traffic and
does no arithmetic — has sat at 134 GB/s where a copy gets 236, with both of
P12-4's hypotheses spent.

content.content:
measured DRAM peak of 236 — 99-103%. The condition is a one-liner: one step
covers the row when `WAVE · VEC · 4 == N/2`, i.e. **`VEC = N / (8 · WAVE)`**,
which at wave64 is `VEC = N/512`: 4 at N=2048, 8 at N=4096, 16 at N=8192. The
previous committed best was 211 GB/s at N=4096 (`vec4` w64) and the kernel had
never been run at any other N; at N=8192 it was **164**, 70% of the bus, which
is the number a real model's decode would have got.

**2. It is the coverage law, applied to the right variable.** §5.1b's
`coverage = min(1, C/gcd(stride, 4096))` is stated for requests in flight; the
stride here is the weight row, `N/2` bytes, and at these N `gcd(N/2, 4096) =
N/2`, so the law says full bandwidth exactly when a step holds the whole row.
That threshold is hit on the nose in all three sweeps. What the law gets wrong
is everything *below* the threshold, where it is far too pessimistic (it
predicts 1/32 of peak at N=8192 `vec1` w32; the measurement is 57%) — expected,
because the law was derived for one wave's requests and here thousands of waves
on adjacent rows partially cover the rotation between them. So: **the law
predicts the cliff edge exactly and the slope not at all.** §6.2 said the law
"predicts the wrong sign" for the wave32 effect. It does, for the wave size.
It is right about the thing the wave size was standing in for.

**3. Same C, different wave size, same bandwidth — to 0.05%.** At N=8192,
`vec8` at wave64 and `vec16` at wave32 both hold 2048 B of a row per step, and
measure **198.83 and 198.93 GB/s**. At N=4096 the two whole-row cells,
`vec8` w64 and `vec16` w32, measure 234.8 and 238.9. That is the direct
falsification of §6.2's wave-size reading: hold C fixed and the wave size
buys nothing.

**4. The 1.07x was a deficit in one cell, not a win in another.** The
wave32-beats-wave64 inversion occurs at exactly one (N, VEC) pair — N=4096,
`VEC=4` — and not at N=2048 or N=8192, where wave64 leads at the same VEC. At
that pair the wave64 kernel takes exactly two steps per row and each step
holds exactly half of it, so every wave in the grid is addressing the same
half of the 4 KB rotation at the same time and the other half's channels sit
idle: §5.1b's mechanism 3, from inside the kernel. Two unrelated changes
each recover it — `ROWS=2` at wave64 (210.6 → 225.5, and ROWS does nothing
in any other cell) and `VEC=8` (→ 234.8, which is the bus). The wave32 arm
was a third. None of them is the fix to reach for; making C the whole row is.

**One more clause the rule needs: every lane must be issuing.** `vec16` at
wave64 and N=4096 has `loadsPerRow = 32` against 64 lanes, so half the wave
is idle. Its C is still a whole row, and it still loses — 212.3 against
234.8 — because it has half as many requests outstanding. The two clauses are
satisfied together by the same equality, which is why the rule is one line and
not two.

**Also: this is why wave64 is the default again.** §6.2's engine rule was
"pin wave32 for the DRAM-resident W4A8 decode GEMV at VEC=4". That is now
superseded: at every N, once VEC is right for wave64, wave32 is equal
(N=4096, 238.9 vs 234.8, inside run-to-run spread) or clearly worse (N=2048,
219.2 vs 243.0 — wave32 satisfies both clauses there and still loses 10%,
which is the one residue this item leaves behind: at equal C and equal lane
occupancy, 64 outstanding requests per wave beat 32).

**Committed numbers, and how to reproduce the rest**: `results/gemv_cold.csv`
holds the default `-coldn 4096`, where the best DRAM-resident decode row is
now **239.1 GB/s** (`subgroup_vec16_w32`, block=1024) against 225.6 before
this item and 211 before §6.2. The N=2048 and N=8192 columns of the table
above are not in that file — one CSV per family means a second N would
overwrite the first — and come from

    go run ./cmd/bench -resultsdir "" -coldfootprints 256 -coldn 8192 \
        -blocks 256 -warmup 5 -iters 20 gemv_cold

with `-coldn 2048` for the other. Both reproduce to ~1% across runs; the
`vec8` w64 cell at N=4096 measured 237.5, 234.8 and 237.8 in three.

**It carries into the cache-resident sweep too, which was not expected.**
The `gemv` family is MALL-resident at these sizes and §6.2 found wave32
*costing* 0.58-0.95x on every row of it. Under the new widths the same sweep's
best W4A8 row at N=4096 goes from **563.5 GB/s** (`vec4`, the committed
previous best) to **734.0** (`vec16_w32`) — **1.30x**. The rule was derived
against DRAM and the MALL has no 4 KB channel rotation to miss, so this is
presumably the plainer half of the same thing (fewer, larger requests per row),
but it was not predicted and it is not explained here.

**What this changes for the engine**: pick `VEC = N/512` per weight matrix at
wave64 — it is a compile-time `-D`, so a real engine ships the two or three
widths its layer shapes need and selects per matrix. The kernel currently
tops out at `VEC=16`, which is N=8192; an N=16384 matrix would want `VEC=32`
(eight `uvec4` per lane) and is a two-line extension of the same macro.

`vec8` at wave64 and `vec16` at wave32 both hold 2048 B of a row per step, and
measure **198.83 and 198.93 GB/s**. At N=4096 the two whole-row cells,
`vec8` w64 and `vec16` w32, measure 234.8 and 238.9. That is the direct
falsification of §6.2's wave-size reading: hold C fixed and the wave size
buys nothing.

**4. The 1.07x was a deficit in one cell, not a win in another.** The
wave32-beats-wave64 inversion occurs at exactly one (N, VEC) pair — N=4096,
`VEC=4` — and not at N=2048 or N=8192, where wave64 leads at the same VEC. At
that pair the wave64 kernel takes exactly two steps per row and each step
holds exactly half of it, so every wave in the grid is addressing the same
half of the 4 KB rotation at the same time and the other half's channels sit
idle: §5.1b's mechanism 3, from inside the kernel. Two unrelated changes
each recover it — `ROWS=2` at wave64 (210.6 → 225.5, and ROWS does nothing
in any other cell) and `VEC=8` (→ 234.8, which is the bus). The wave32 arm
was a third. None of them is the fix to reach for; making C the whole row is.

**One more clause the rule needs: every lane must be issuing.** `vec16` at
wave64 and N=4096 has `loadsPerRow = 32` against 64 lanes, so half the wave
is idle. Its C is still a whole row, and it still loses — 212.3 against
234.8 — because it has half as many requests outstanding. The two clauses are
satisfied together by the same equality, which is why the rule is one line and
not two.

**Also: this is why wave64 is the default again.** §6.2's engine rule was
"pin wave32 for the DRAM-resident W4A8 decode GEMV at VEC=4". That is now
superseded: at every N, once VEC is right for wave64, wave32 is equal
(N=4096, 238.9 vs 234.8, inside run-to-run spread) or clearly worse (N=2048,
219.2 vs 243.0 — wave32 satisfies both clauses there and still loses 10%,
which is the one residue this item leaves behind: at equal C and equal lane
occupancy, 64 outstanding requests per wave beat 32).

**Committed numbers, and how to reproduce the rest**: `results/gemv_cold.csv`
holds the default `-coldn 4096`, where the best DRAM-resident decode row is
now **239.1 GB/s** (`subgroup_vec16_w32`, block=1024) against 225.6 before
this item and 211 before §6.2. The N=2048 and N=8192 columns of the table
above are not in that file — one CSV per family means a second N would
overwrite the first — and come from

    go run ./cmd/bench -resultsdir "" -coldfootprints 256 -coldn 8192 \
        -blocks 256 -warmup 5 -iters 20 gemv_cold

with `-coldn 2048` for the other. Both reproduce to ~1% across runs; the
`vec8` w64 cell at N=4096 measured 237.5, 234.8 and 237.8 in three.

**It carries into the cache-resident sweep too, which was not expected.**
The `gemv` family is MALL-resident at these sizes and §6.2 found wave32
*costing* 0.58-0.95x on every row of it. Under the new widths the same sweep's
best W4A8 row at N=4096 goes from **563.5 GB/s** (`vec4`, the committed
previous best) to **734.0** (`vec16_w32`) — **1.30x**. The rule was derived
against DRAM and the MALL has no 4 KB channel rotation to miss, so this is
presumably the plainer half of the same thing (fewer, larger requests per row),
but it was not predicted and it is not explained here.

**What this changes for the engine**: pick `VEC = N/512` per weight matrix at
wave64 — it is a compile-time `-D`, so a real engine ships the two or three
widths its layer shapes need and selects per matrix. The kernel currently
tops out at `VEC=16`, which is N=8192; an N=16384 matrix would want `VEC=32`
(eight `uvec4` per lane) and is a two-line extension of the same macro.

---
name: llm-resident-run
description: The whole-model runs (`cmd/llm -resident`, `-graph`, `-gen`, `-ppl`, `cmd/serve -llm`, `TestGraphLogits`) stage 82-83 GB of qwen3.8-flash-next; what they cost in time and RAM, and why nothing else can run beside them.
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Since L8a/L8b the dense banks are int8 rather than halves and residency is
81.89 GB with the head** (`-dense` 4.32 GB); `LLM_DENSE_FP16=1` puts every
block back on the old halves and restores the old sizes exactly, which is how
the two are compared. **A decode token is 31.7 ms and residency 79.85 GB as of
L8c-7 (2026-09-17)** with all five 4.5-bit families named in
`LLM_DENSE_BANK` — 40.5 ms at L8e, 33.3 at L8c-6, ~134 before L7d — so `-n 64`
is a ~2.0 s tail on top of staging. Without `LLM_DENSE_BANK` the run is still
L8a's int8 bank at 81.89 GB and 40.5 ms.

**Do not schedule a whole-model run above ~2560 rows**: at 48 layers
`-graph -tokens 3072` (or `-ppl -ctx 4096`) **never returns** — it stalls
inside the driver's submit with one host thread at 100% and the GPU at 2-3%,
and the shim's 20 s fence timeout never fires, so it hangs indefinitely rather
than erroring. 2048 and 2560 are fine; the 4-layer prefix is fine at 4096.
This is a known open question in `research/llm-vertical.md`, not a mistake to re-discover.

`go run ./cmd/llm -resident` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6a) stages every layer
of all five blocks: **84.20 GB of device buffers (82.40 since L8a), ~35 s wall
clock**, and it
ends with about 41 GB of MemAvailable left on this 117.7 GiB machine. Peak
host memory is separate — the dense blocks dequantise to f32 before packing,
and the 36 DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once — which is
why the tool stages dense first and the 77 GB expert bank last.

**Why:** it is the only thing in the repo that takes most of the machine, so a
second GPU or large-allocation job started beside it will either fail to
allocate or perturb the timing it prints. `-bank N,N,...` restages just the
bank, which is the cheap way to vary residency; `-dense` is the 6.8 GB half
and runs in 8 s.

`go run ./cmd/llm -graph` and `go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphLogits` (added
2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6b) are the same weight but **85.47 GB**, because they add
the 1.27 GB lm head; `-tokens 2048` adds another ~1.1 GB of arenas. Staging is
---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

---
name: llm-resident-run
description: The whole-model runs (`cmd/llm -resident`, `-graph`, `-gen`, `-ppl`, `cmd/serve -llm`, `TestGraphLogits`) stage 82-83 GB of qwen3.8-flash-next; what they cost in time and RAM, and why nothing else can run beside them.
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Since L8a/L8b the dense banks are int8 rather than halves and residency is
81.89 GB with the head** (`-dense` 4.32 GB); `LLM_DENSE_FP16=1` puts every
block back on the old halves and restores the old sizes exactly, which is how
the two are compared. **A decode token is 31.7 ms and residency 79.85 GB as of
L8c-7 (2026-09-17)** with all five 4.5-bit families named in
`LLM_DENSE_BANK` — 40.5 ms at L8e, 33.3 at L8c-6, ~134 before L7d — so `-n 64`
is a ~2.0 s tail on top of staging. Without `LLM_DENSE_BANK` the run is still
L8a's int8 bank at 81.89 GB and 40.5 ms.

**Do not schedule a whole-model run above ~2560 rows**: at 48 layers
`-graph -tokens 3072` (or `-ppl -ctx 4096`) **never returns** — it stalls
inside the driver's submit with one host thread at 100% and the GPU at 2-3%,
and the shim's 20 s fence timeout never fires, so it hangs indefinitely rather
than erroring. 2048 and 2560 are fine; the 4-layer prefix is fine at 4096.
This is a known open question in `research/llm-vertical.md`, not a mistake to re-discover.

`go run ./cmd/llm -resident` (added 2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6a) stages every layer
of all five blocks: **84.20 GB of device buffers (82.40 since L8a), ~35 s wall
clock**, and it
ends with about 41 GB of MemAvailable left on this 117.7 GiB machine. Peak
host memory is separate — the dense blocks dequantise to f32 before packing,
and the 36 DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once — which is
why the tool stages dense first and the 77 GB expert bank last.

**Why:** it is the only thing in the repo that takes most of the machine, so a
second GPU or large-allocation job started beside it will either fail to
allocate or perturb the timing it prints. `-bank N,N,...` restages just the
bank, which is the cheap way to vary residency; `-dense` is the 6.8 GB half
and runs in 8 s.

`go run ./cmd/llm -graph` and `go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphLogits` (added
2026-09-16, research/llm-vertical.md L6b) are the same weight but **85.47 GB**, because they add
the 1.27 GB lm head; `-tokens 2048` adds another ~1.1 GB of arenas. Staging is
---
name: strix-halo-bench-runs
description: "How the strix-halo-vulkan benchmark suite is run and how long each family takes, plus the run-quality conventions the repo's docs expect."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c27486f-644d-4f43-a0b0-6ebe2136679b
  modified: 2026-09-18T12:55:03.680Z
---

`go run ./cmd/bench -blocks 32,64,128,256,512,1024 <family>` — the non-default
block list is what every committed `results/*.csv` was measured with, so keep
it if rows are to stay comparable. `go generate ./...` first if any `.comp`
changed (`*.spv` is gitignored). As of 2026-09-13 the `moe` family is ~9
minutes / 896 rows; it prints its summary tables only at the end, so there is
no progress output to poll — run it in the foreground with a long timeout.
The `bank` family (added 2026-09-15, research/llm-vertical.md L0a) is the odd one out: its 72
timed cells are seconds, but `go run ./cmd/bench -bankgib 64 -bankreadmib 1024
bank` first allocates 64 GiB in 19 buffers and writes one word per 4 KB page,
which is most of its ~3-minute wall clock. Check `free -g` has the headroom
before starting it.

**A whole-model tok/s number is only comparable against a control run the
same hour** (P1c, 2026-09-18): with an identical binary the decode step
measured 30.51 ms one day and 39.20 the next — every *dense-bank* kernel
1.6-1.9x slower (dn.qkv 115→206 us, head 1964→3531) while every MoE
expert-bank rung was unchanged. Suspected GTT page fragmentation of the
float-staged dense banks (32-day uptime, swap 100% full); unprovable without
root. **And a difference below ~0.5 tok/s needs interleaved A/B/A/B pairs, not one
pair** (P3, 2026-09-18): three pairs of the same two banks gave −0.06, +0.14
and +0.05 tok/s, so either single pair would have reported a signed number
where the truth was a within-arm spread of 0.31 against a real difference of
~0.04. Quote the means and the within-arm spread, not one delta.

So when measuring a decode/prefill change, rebuild yesterday's code in
a worktree (`.spv` are gitignored — regenerate or copy them) and run both
binaries back to back; never quote a delta against a prior day's CSV. Also:
run 1 of a freshly staged graph diverges from runs 2+ at ~1.6e-5 in the
logits (research/p1c-prerecorded-decode.md finding 4) — warm the graph once
before any bitwise comparison.

content.content:
instead of reporting a plausible bandwidth.

#### Mechanism 1: channel coverage — 2-4x, and it hits contiguous reads

The interleave on this part is 256 B across **sixteen** channels, i.e. a
**4 KB rotation** (what a 256-bit LPDDR5X bus of 16-bit sub-channels gives).
Row *k* starts at `k*stride`, so row starts land only on the multiples of
`g = gcd(stride, 4096)` inside one rotation, and each row covers `rowBytes`
from its start. When `rowBytes < g` the union of them **never addresses some
channels at all**, and the achievable fraction of peak is exactly the
fraction of channels touched:

> **coverage = min(1, rowBytes / gcd(stride, 4096))**

1024 B rows, 64 MiB touched, GB/s (`model` is the formula; rows are how many
distinct rows one request spans):

| rows/req | 1024 | 1280 | 2048 | 3072 | 4096* | 5120 | 9216 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **model** | 1.00 | 1.00 | **0.50** | 1.00 | **0.25** | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| 1 (contiguous) | 243 | 241 | **120** | 242 | **61** | 245 | 239 |
| 4 | 243 | 241 | 122 | 243 | 61 | 245 | 239 |
| 16 | 234 | 238 | 113 | 233 | 55 | 237 | 231 |
| 32 | 230 | 239 | 113 | 234 | 58 | 238 | 232 |
| 64 (gather) | 232 | 240 | 120 | 237 | 59 | 242 | 235 |

The model holds to within 2% at every point, for every shape. Note which
strides are the bad ones — 2048, 4096, 8192, the ones a tidy allocator picks
— while 1280 and 3072 are perfect. At 2048 B rows (a K=1024 fp16 weight row)
it is the same law one notch weaker: 243 GB/s at stride 2048, **123 at 4096**,
242 at 6144, **121 at 8192**.

None of this is visible to anything §2.3 measured: a K=4096 fp16 row is
8192 B, already ≥ any `g`, so its coverage is full at every stride.

#### Mechanism 2: per-request aliasing — up to 1.32x, and it needs a gather

With coverage full (8192 B rows), a stride that is a multiple of 4 KB costs a
contiguous read *nothing* and costs progressively more the more rows one
request spans. 64 MiB touched, GB/s:

| rows/req | 8192* | 8208 | 8256 | 8320 | 8448 | 8704 | 9216 | 10240 | 11264 | 12288* | 14336 | 16384* |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (contiguous) | 243 | 238 | 238 | 240 | 242 | 243 | 244 | 244 | 243 | 242 | 243 | 243 |
| 4 | 231 | 226 | 228 | 230 | 236 | 240 | 244 | 245 | 242 | 232 | 245 | 233 |
| 16 | 205 | 210 | 216 | 229 | 236 | 237 | 237 | 238 | 236 | 202 | 236 | 202 |
| 32 | 204 | 205 | 214 | 238 | 235 | 236 | 238 | 238 | 236 | 201 | 236 | 200 |
| 64 (gather) | **182** | 198 | 230 | 237 | 230 | 233 | **239** | 237 | 238 | **174** | 238 | **180** |

(* = multiple of 4 KB. Identical to within 1% at 256 MiB touched, so this is
a property of DRAM and not of the footprint.)

**The period is 4 KB, not the 2 KB §2.3 inferred.** With nine strides inside
one rotation the sweep is unambiguous: 10240 and 14336 **are** multiples of
2 KB and run at the full rate, while 8192, 12288 and 16384 — the multiples of
4 KB — are the only slow strides. And recovery inside a period is complete by
+128-256 B, then flat: +16 B gets a third of it, +64 B most of it, and
everything from +128 B to +3072 B is within noise of the best.

#### The MALL behaves differently on both counts

At 16 MiB touched a pure read delivers **930-965 GB/s** — above the 805 GB/s
§0.4 measured with a read+write copy — and:

- it is **immune to the gather penalty**: the 64-row gather measures 824-896
  GB/s at *every* stride, aliased or not, i.e. a flat ~0.93x of the other
with the identical twins 2.3% apart.

#### Mechanism 3: the traversal — the coverage law is about what is *in flight*

**[measured]** The one pattern the sweep above could not reach was
concurrent-but-contiguous requests from *different* waves at an aliased
stride: every shape there varies the addresses inside one request, and the
contiguous shape deliberately walks along a row, so consecutive waves are
never a stride apart. `CROSS_WAVE` on `strided_read.comp` swaps the two loop
orders over the (row-group, column-block) grid so consecutive requests
advance down the rows instead of along one. It is a permutation of exactly
the same (row, chunk) set — same bytes, same footprint, same instruction
count, same host checksum — and the only thing that moves is which addresses
are outstanding at the same moment.

It is the largest effect in this family, it **subsumes mechanism 1**, and it
fires with no padding involved at all.

8192 B rows, 64 MiB touched, contiguous 1 KB requests, GB/s:

| stride | 8192* | 8208 | 8256 | 8320 | 8448 | 8704 | 9216 | 10240 | 11264 | 12288* | 14336 | 16384* |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gcd(stride,4096)` | 4096 | 16 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 1024 | 4096 | 2048 | 4096 |
| **model** | **0.25** | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | **0.50** | 1.00 | **0.25** | **0.50** | **0.25** |
| walk along a row | 243 | 238 | 238 | 240 | 242 | 243 | 244 | 244 | 243 | 243 | 243 | 243 |

---
name: spec-loop-run
description: How to run the speculative decode loop in strix-halo-vulkan (`cmd/llm -spec`), what it costs, and the two things to read before believing its numbers.
metadata:
  type: project
---

`go run ./cmd/llm -spec` (added 2026-09-19, P5c) stages the 48-layer trunk
**and** the 1.92 GB draft head and then runs two arms interleaved in one
process — a plain greedy loop and the speculative one — because P1c's
environment finding means a decode rate from a different day is not a control.
**~85 GB, ~31 s to stage the trunk plus ~1 s for the draft, then ~5 s per
128-token arm**; `-spec-passes 2` (the default) is four arms, so budget ~1200 s
and pass the shard path, not the directory (see [[llm-resident-run]]).

- `-ctx 512` is the short arm; `-spec-prefix N` prompts with the first N tokens
  of `-ppl-file` instead of `-prompt`, which is the long arm. **Never above
  `-ctx 2048`** — the draft head refuses, for the reason in
  [[mtp-draft-head-run]].
- `-layers 4` is the 9 GB plumbing check: the mechanics work and the
  acceptance rate is 0%, because the draft head was trained against 48 layers.
- `SPEC_PLAIN_ONLY=1` drops the speculative arm and runs the plain loop

### 2.14 The GEMM's epilogue: the fp32 store costs the pipe nothing, the sawtooth is ≤ 5%, and the two passes that read the fp32 C fused into it — **done** ✅ (2026-09-30)

**Question** (KERNELS.md G3, hypotheses H4 and H5 of the reopened
vertical): the shipped GEMM (`dit_gemm_wg128x256_lds_w32`, §2.9/§2.10)
ends with 16 fp32 accumulator tiles a wave stored row-major — 128
`buffer_store_b32` a lane, two 64 B segments each — and H4 priced that
operand, once a layer, and the qkv projection after each move stalled behind
the writes draining. `cmd/llm -depth -ubatch` found it by staging wide arenas
and prefilling narrow — the cost followed the arena, not the prefill — and the
per-label diff put all of it on `move`, `dn.qkv` and `attn.qkv`. The port now
pads to the row block, as the MoE's always did, and
`TestInPortPadsTheRunNotTheArena` asserts it, because the old padding was
*correct* and no tolerance could see it. Two smaller exact changes ride along:
**`hc.cn` is a workgroup a (token, stream) again at ≤ 64 rows** (25.0 → 7.0 µs,
1.06x of a token — P11's workgroup a token is one workgroup on forty CUs at
decode), and **`attn.select`'s emit walks blocks rather than cells** (68 → 55
µs at 128k). `-llm-batch` stays 4096; 8192 is now purely a memory decision.

6 §5.2
